articles.title: NFL Catchup: Kyler Murray In Concussion Protocol; Eagles Place Landon Dickerson On IR
articles.summary: Here's the latest from around the NFL on Monday.
articles.body: Week 1 is in the books, but the injury report is just getting started as several teams spent Monday sorting through the fallout from their openers. The Philadelphia Eagles lost starting left guard Landon Dickerson to injured reserve after he admitted to playing through pain in Sunday's win over the Washington Commanders. In Minnesota, Kyler Murray's concussion from Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers has left his Week 2 status very much in doubt. There was better news elsewhere, though, as running back TreVeyon Henderson looks set to return to practice for the New England Patriots, and Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey appears to have avoided a long-term injury. Here's the latest from around the NFL on Monday. Kyler Murray In Concussion Protocol Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray left Sunday's season opener against the Green Bay Packers after taking a violent hit to the head while sliding. Murray was placed in concussion protocol, leaving his status for Week 2 in serious doubt. Speaking to reporters Monday afternoon, head coach Kevin O’Connell said Murray remains in concussion protocol. He had no update on his availability against the Chicago Bears, but said the team will monitor his progress throughout the week. Murray struggled in his first start in purple and gold, throwing an interception on his opening drive. He then exited on the third drive after suffering a concussion, and his timeline for a return remains unclear. If Murray is unable to clear protocol in time, Carson Wentz would seemingly start, with J.J. McCarthy serving as the backup. Wentz is coming off a strong performance against the Packers, throwing three touchdowns after stepping in for the injured Murray. Landon Dickerson Placed On Injured Reserve The Eagles are going to be without one of their starting offensive linemen for at least a month. Philadelphia is placing left guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve with a knee injury, a move that will sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for a minimum of four games. Dickerson struggled in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders, later admitting on 94 WIP in Philadelphia that he'd been playing injured, which affected his level of play. "I played like s--- yesterday," Dickerson said. "I was a complete liability yesterday and again, that was my fault. I know I said I shouldn't be out there until I feel healthy. A few weeks ago I got rolled up on in practice; I thought as the week went by it would get better and it didn't." Dickerson said he underwent imaging on the knee Monday before the team settled on injured reserve as the path forward, as he later described the injury as a bone bruise. "Bone bruising doesn’t really heal if you keep banging it and doing stuff. It’s one of those things where you have to shut it down and not do anything," Dickerson said, remaining optimistic that the injury won't linger once he's off IR. The move continues a rough stretch of lower-body injuries for the 27-year-old, who had meniscus surgery last August that he admitted he probably returned from too soon. With Dickerson out, second-year lineman Drew Kendall is the favorite to step into the starting lineup at left guard, though rookie Willie Lampkin could also factor in. TreVeyon Henderson Expected To Return To Practice The New England Patriots are coming off a brutal Week 1 loss against the Seattle Seahawks, but reinforcements could be on the way for the offense. Even with injury setbacks in the receiving room, running back TreVeyon Henderson could return on Sunday. When speaking to reporters on Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel said that Henderson will be returning to practice this week. This is a positive sign, as he hasn’t practiced since August 24 during training camp. With star wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve, bringing an explosive playmaker like Henderson back into the mix is pivotal for the offense. The Patriots offense was limited to just 10 points in the loss to the Seahawks. If Henderson isn't cleared for Sunday, expect Rhamondre Stevenson to handle a heavy bell-cow workload once again. Ladd McConkey Injury Update After taking a hit in the middle of the field, Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey left with a chest injury and didn’t return. Head coach Jim Harbaugh updated reporters on Monday afternoon, describing it as a rib injury and that he’s day-to-day. McConkey’s availability against the Las Vegas Raiders is up in the air, but he appears to have avoided a stint on injured reserve. While the exact nature of McConkey’s rib injury remains unclear, he put together a strong performance before exiting against the Arizona Cardinals. McConkey was able to haul in five receptions for 82 yards and a touchdown.Should McConkey miss time, expect Quentin Johnston, Tre Harris, and rookie Brenen Thompson to step into larger roles this weekend.

articles.title: Novig CEO Says Sydney Sweeney Drove ‘Visuals and Messaging’ of Nude Ad
articles.summary: “We never intended to portray female sports," Jacob Fortinsky told FOS.
articles.body:
Last week, sports-only prediction market Novig released an advertisement featuring actress Sydney Sweeney, who appeared totally nude save for a series of strategically placed sports equipment. Since then, scores of professional female athletes from around the world have ripped the spot , saying it hypersexualizes women's relationship to sports.

Novig CEO Jacob Fortinsky responded to the backlash onstage Tuesday at the Front Office Sports Asset Class event in New York.

"As a company we're hugely supportive of women's sports, and it's a huge component of our platform," Fortinsky said. "We never intended to portray female sports. Sydney is an actress, the biggest movie star in the world. We're a prediction market focused on sports. That is the story she was communicating."

He indicated that Sweeney, who is an equity holder in Novig, served as the campaign's creative lead: "It was a very exciting process to work with her, both on the commercial side and the creative side. It really was Sydney who was driving a lot of the visuals and the messaging."

The goal of the ad, Fortinsky said, was to "introduce [Novig] to the nation" ahead of football season and "close the gap from a brand-awareness perspective" between it and prediction-market leaders, like Kalshi and Polymarket. "We asked ourselves who would be the best person to grab the attention of the public to make Novig a household name," he explained. "Sydney approached us, but from there it was a very obvious decision."

On X/Twitter, Novig's post sharing the ad has garnered more than 12 million views; on Instagram, it has surpassed 47 million. That's roughly 400 times higher than the company's next-most-recent video post on the platform.

Novig formally launched in August. Fortinsky told FOS at Asset Class that the company "just passed a billion dollars in cumulative volume," claiming that marks the fastest start of any prediction market in history.

For the Novig CEO, the attention from the Sweeney spot outweighs the pushback. "There are a lot of people that have feelings about Sydney as a person that predate this campaign. Working with her, we obviously expected the people who already hate her would be loud and vocal," Fortinsky said. "Ultimately, I think she did a great job at conveying the essence of our company and we've been very happy with how positive the feedback has been overall."

articles.title: Josh Allen Leads The Charge As Multiple NFL Players Push For All-Grass Fields
articles.summary: There's little debate when it comes to NFL players' preference for playing on grass versus artificial surfaces.
articles.body: For Josh Allen, the grass is most definitely greener across the street. As the Buffalo Bills moved closer to their first regular-season game Thursday in their new Highmark Stadium, the quarterback looked forward to not having to deal with the added wear and tear his body previously experienced playing on the artificial turf of the team’s now-demolished old facility. "I’ve gotten numerous, numerous burns on my legs from artificial turf, to the point I can’t sleep at night because it’s bubbling over. It’s very painful," Allen said, noting he still feels it after the Bills practice on the turf inside their fieldhouse. "If I could snap my fingers and make every field grass, that’s what I would do for sure." The new Bills stadium and Allen’s comments reflect an increasingly heated debate in the league over whether teams should play on artificial turf or natural grass. It follows a World Cup in which tournament organizers mandated converting seven NFL stadiums from turf to grass, only to switch back to artificial surfaces for the pro football season. Players Overwhelmingly Support Grass NFL players and their union overwhelmingly favor natural grass and are perplexed about why the league’s billionaire owners can’t do what FIFA did for the World Cup. "It’s a little bizarre, but what can you expect?" 49ers defensive lineman Nick Bosa said. As with most debates, it’s about money. Though the NFL does not provide cost figures, it's widely accepted that artificial turf is much more affordable than grass, which requires year-round maintenance and constant resodding. NFL grass fields generally have a lifespan of about seven events. Artificial fields also require some maintenance to replace infill, and generally have a lifespan of between three to seven years. That still doesn't square with players, even as the NFL continues trending toward artificial surfaces. "Natural grass isn’t out of reach. Prioritizing players shouldn’t be either!" Colts running back Jonathan Taylor posted on his X account with the hashtag "WorthTheCost." With Buffalo, 16 of the NFL’s 30 facilities will feature grass this season, including Green Bay’s Lambeau Field, which is made up of 95% grass and reinforced with polyethylene fibers. Of the 18 NFL facilities built since 2000, 11 have artificial surfaces, and those don't include Carolina and Tennessee, which recently made the switch to turf. Cost and maintenance appear to play more of a factor than geography, with six of the NFL’s seven coldest markets and all three Florida-based teams featuring grass surfaces. Where there is consensus is that NFL playing surfaces are far more advanced today than 50 years ago when several teams, starting with the Houston Oilers, played on AstroTurf — essentially a thinly padded carpet laid over concrete or asphalt. NFL/NFLPA Set Standards For All Fields Nick Pappas, the NFL’s director of field surfaces, said the advancements in turf technology are night and day since the AstroTurf era. The focus now, he said, is the NFL and NFLPA working with all turf manufacturers to establish standards for surfaces based on player feedback and metrics from testing conducted by the league. This led to the league and union jointly releasing a series of standardized playing surface requirements each facility must meet by 2028. The list of criteria covering both playing and practice surfaces includes minimum standards for impact, traction, and guidelines for when to resurface. The objective is to achieve as much consistency as possible across all 30 NFL playing surfaces, whether grass or artificial. "The goal is that we take the emotions out of the material makeup," Pappas said. "What the composition of the field is should only be secondary to how the field performs." In the past, Pappas said, the guidelines for field composition were easy to comply with, leading to teams choosing their turf by cutting the best deal with a manufacturer. Now, the league and union are having manufacturers present their products for testing before being certified. "That’s really the course correction," Pappas said. "It’s, bring us a product once you believe you’ve met (the criteria). And then we’ll run it through the wringer and get it in front of our athlete and ensure that we feel comfortable putting it into play." The NFL cites its own studies in saying there has been no significant difference in injury rates when comparing artificial turf and grass over the past three seasons. And last season’s lower-extremity injury rate was half of the average level that occurred from 2018-22. And yet players, and even some NFL owners, prefer grass. That was the case in Las Vegas, where Raiders managing general partner Mark Davis cited player safety as one reason to install grass despite moving into an indoor facility. The same applied in Buffalo, where owner Terry Pegula considered installing natural grass in the team’s old facility before electing to wait until the new one was built. Already Resodding In Buffalo The Bills have encountered a few hiccups in making the switch, and that's despite installing heating coils, grow lights and ventilation systems to spur growth. The team recently elected to resod its entire field ahead of schedule after divots and worn areas became exposed after just two preseason games and two practices. The Bills elected to resod after their final preseason game to take advantage of a three-plus-week window before their home opener. And they're expected to resod the field at last once more before the season is over. Pappas called it a trial and error process, because there’s a learning curve involved to determine how grass reacts to a new environment. "Obviously, we were seeing a grass that maybe didn’t have the strength that everybody had hoped for and was pulling apart a little more than expected or preferred," said Pappas, who personally inspected the Bills' field before and after the team’s preseason finale last month. "They’ll continue to adapt and make adjustments as they need to. ... And I do anticipate things will continue to improve." The NFLPA, meantime, applauded the Bills for installing grass in the first place, and sticking with it despite the additional costs involved. Cost isn’t an issue as far as Bills President Pete Guelli is concerned. "I understand the economics of why people want an artificial turf field," Guelli told The Associated Press. "But if you’re really putting your players first, there’s no other choice but grass." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Most common players on eliminated teams from Week 1 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues — plus FAB waiver wire advice
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski goes over the most common players on eliminated teams after Week 1 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues.
articles.body:
Every week I'll examine the most common NFL players on the teams eliminated in Yahoo Death Leagues, trying to figure out where the puck is headed. I will also offer some FAB advice ($1,000 cap is the Yahoo default), but please remember this area is highly context-sensitive and manager-specific.

If you're new to this format, it's critical to understand that waiver strategy is significantly different in the world of Death Leagues.

You can often win a traditional fantasy league with modest help from the waiver wire, maybe a timely pickup or two. Sure, it's great if you crush the market and land the right guys — the best managers will always aim to be smart on the wire — but if your drafted team stays healthy and runs pure, some years that might be enough.

Immediate needs vs. playing the long game

In Death Leagues, the eventual winning manager will have assembled a MONSTER team at the end of the year, a juggernaut, a Pro Bowl-type of roster. And the way you build that beast is usually by having resources all season — not by using the majority of your FAB on a tantalizing early star. It's pivotal that you understand that the waiver wire should get stronger and stronger every week in Death leagues, because the eliminated manager is coming from a smaller and smaller league size every week.

Unless you have a draft touched by the fantasy angels, you are unlikely to win a Death League without a successful and careful waiver-wire strategy.

My Death League strategy is centered on the concept that I like my squad early in the year and I am confident I can beat at least one team per week while the field of opponents is large. Therefore, while I will dip my toes into the FAB market in the first quarter of the season, my primary goal is to keep major reserves in play for later in the year, when bye weeks hit and injuries are more prevalent — and the pool of opponents is smaller (so advancing is harder, in theory). Again, I urge you to remember: the waiver wire in Death Leagues gets stronger as the year gets deeper, a key reason to be judicious with your resources.

Not everyone will share my strategy, of course. If you want to chase major improvements and use the bulk of your FAB to load up quickly, then shoot your shot. Play the strategy you're comfortable with. Just understand that my recommendations are predicated on being careful early, and if you prefer something more aggressive, you'll have to jump the numbers up. You know your room better than an outsider does.

I will offer weekly FAB recommendations in three buckets:

Proactive : This means you highly covet this player, perhaps might even need this player. I realize these offers might not win if someone in your league is lighting money on fire, but as described above, that's often a short-sighted mistake in this format.

Reactive : This means you desire the player but the offer has to make sense for your short- or long-term strategy.

Keep Them Honest : This is an offer that is not designed to win, but might surprisingly land a player if your opponents are distracted by other talent available or unexpectedly passive that week. I often compare notes with other experienced Death League players and we're surprised at how often the Keep Them Honest offers actually win (this is also a portable strategy for regular season-long leagues; you never know when strange market behavior will come about).

One last note: understand that the FAB recommendations are with the assumption that you won't be making offers for every available player.

10 most common players on eliminated teams

We've seen this story before — Chase had a similar no-show in Week 1 last year, despite playing almost all of the snaps. It's probably a Bengals problem more than a Chase problem. No reason to change our view of the player.

Did Sean Payton make a mistake giving the play-calling duties to first-time coordinator Davis Webb? Waddle had a 1-2-0 nightmare at Kansas City, and perhaps most alarming, had just two targets. Sometimes it takes time for players to adjust to new surroundings, I suppose.

It was a nightmare show in Kansas City, and most of the early schedule is challenging. Nix also showed little as a runner Monday night, which hurts his floor.

He had the backfield essentially to himself, though Josh Allen did steal two rushing touchdowns. Houston was a tough assignment; Detroit on Thursday is an easier draw. Cook retains his set-and-forget status.

He was open for a long touchdown, but Drake Maye underthrew the pass. Brown later suffered a high ankle sprain, likely to cost him six weeks. Death Leagues are all about right now, so Brown offers must be tempered.

It was a pesky and sluggish opener (just 28 yards, one drop), though the Dallas defense didn't help the cause (the Giants ran all over the unit). Better days are ahead for a Dallas offense tied to a star QB and a tight target tree.

articles.title: It's Roberto Clemente Day! Pirates Legend's MLB Career By The Numbers
articles.summary: It's Roberto Clemente Day! Here's the Pittsburgh Pirates legend and Baseball Hall of Famer's MLB career by the numbers.
articles.body: Everybody who takes the field in Tuesday night's MLB games will have a No. 21 patch on their jersey. That's because Sept. 15 is Roberto Clemente Day, a day of remembrance for Pittsburgh Pirates legend and Baseball Hall of Famer Roberto Clemente and his charitable contributions, a legacy that lives on through the Roberto Clemente Foundation. As for the right fielder's on-field success, Clemente, who wore No. 21, was a force to be reckoned with. Here's his MLB career (1955-72) by the numbers: 1A: Clemente is first in Pirates history with 3,000 hits, 4,492 total bases and 2,154 singles. 1B: On that note, he's one of 33 players to hit the 3,000-hit mark. 2A: Clemente was part of the Pirates' 1960 and 1971 World Series triumphs. 2B: Clemente led the National League in hits twice: in 1964 and 1967. 2C: His career 95 wins above replacement are second in Pirates history and 37th in MLB altogether. 3: Clemente is third in Pirates history with 1,416 runs scored, 1,305 RBIs, 440 doubles and 166 triples. 4: He led the NL in batting average in four seasons: 1961, 1964, 1965 and 1967. 8.2: Clemente led NL position players with 8.2 wins above replacement in 1968. 10: Clemente logged a double-digit number of triples in 10 seasons, including leading the NL with 12 triples in 1969. 12: The number of Gold Gloves he won. 15: The number of All-Star nods he received. 18: Each of Clemente's 18 seasons in the sport were spent with the Pirates. 200: He logged 200-plus hits in four seasons: 1961, 1964, 1966 and 1967. 240: The number of home runs Clemente hit. 300: Clemente finished with a .300 or higher batting average in 13 of his 18 seasons in the sport. 317: Clemente was a career .317 regular-season hitter, tied with Joe Harris for 66th in MLB history. 318: He was a career .318 postseason hitter in 113 plate appearances. 1966: Clemente won the 1966 NL MVP Award. 1971: Clemente was the 1971 World Series MVP, totaling 12 hits, two home runs and four RBIs while posting a .414/.452/.759 slash line in the seven-game series against the Baltimore Orioles. 1973: MLB renamed the "Commissioner’s Award" the "Roberto Clemente Award" in 1973, which is an award "given annually to a player who demonstrates the values Hall of Famer Roberto Clemente displayed in his commitment to community and understanding the value of helping others." Each of MLB's 30 teams have a nominee for the award, with the league office naming one recipient of the honor during the World Series of that particular year. 2,305: Clemente is first in MLB history with 2,305 appearances in right field. 2,433: Clemente and Honus Wagner are tied for first in Pirates history with 2,433 games played.

articles.title: Why Female Athletes Are Fighting Back Against Sydney Sweeney’s New Ad
articles.summary: The backlash against the new Novig ad is the latest example of female athletes fighting to be valued for their athletic abilities, and not for how they look.
articles.body:
Female athletes are speaking out against a new ad featuring the actress Sydney Sweeney scantily clad in various sports gear. The backlash is the latest example of female athletes fighting to be valued for their athletic abilities, and not for how they look.

The ad, for sports betting platform Novig, features Sweeney appearing to be naked, with various pieces of sports equipment strategically covering her body. The ad debuted on September 9, and Novig said in a press release that it was their "first national brand campaign." In the same release, Sweeney, who is also an equity holder in Novig, said, "The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge."

Dozens of high-profile female athletes have already spoken out against the ad. Ariane Titmus, an Olympic swimming champion, described the ad as "a kick in the face to every woman who has dedicated her life to perfecting her craft."

Amy Hunt, a British track star and Olympic medalist, gave her opinion of the ad on Good Morning Britain "When we're trying to provide role models for young people and young women in sport, we really want to show that it's about what your body can do, not so much what it looks like." She added that she thought the ad could deter young women from pursuing sports.

Other female athletes agree that the ad detracts from what it takes to be a female athlete. In an Instagram post, American gymnast Gracie Kramer shared footage of herself competing, along with the description, "This is what a woman in sport looks like." Her post has received more than 1.2 million likes. According to The Guardian , hundreds of athletes followed her lead and have posted photos of themselves competing.

Novig did not respond to a request for comment about the female athletes' reaction to the ad.

Female Athletes Have Been Fighting This Battle For Decades

The backlash against the ad isn't just about the nudity. It reflects a decades-long struggle over how women in sports are portrayed. Scantily clad women were once routinely used to sell male-oriented products ranging from cars and auto parts to hamburgers. Major brands have largely moved away from this advertising strategy, but female athletes continue to struggle to escape the persistent focus on their appearance. Here's some background.

In 2004, FIFA president Sepp Blatter suggested female soccer players could increase the game's popularity by wearing sexier outfits. "Let the women play in more feminine clothes, like they do in volleyball," Blatter proposed . "They could for example, have tighter shorts. Female players are pretty," he added. At the time, women's beach volleyball uniforms were limited to a maximum of 2.8 inches on the sides. The volleyball rules were later modified to give players more options of what they could wear.

Media coverage also focused on female athletes' appearance. Between 2012 and 2016, women appeared on only 10% of Sports Illustrated and ESPN The Magazine covers, but when they appeared, they were more likely to be shown in sexually objectifying poses and scant clothing. Male athletes were more often depicted in their uniform and actively playing their sports.

There are signs this is changing. A review of 64 studies published between 1994 and 2024 found that although sports media have generally focused more on female athletes' appearance and sexuality and less on their athletic performance, more recent studies show there has been greater emphasis on women's athletic abilities and accomplishments. Nonetheless, sexualized portrayals haven't completely disappeared.

That history and recent progress helps explain why the Sweeney ad struck a nerve. Female athletes see it as a step backward.

Nonetheless, selling products with scantily clad women may still be effective. Consumer research company Zappi tested reaction to the Novig ad, by surveying 200 nationally representative online gamblers. A whopping 73.4% of men said the ad made them more likely to choose Novig, compared with 42.0% of women. Meanwhile, 32.8% of women said the ad made them less likely to choose the brand, versus just 8.4% of men. "That suggests the creative may be doing what it was designed to do with its core male audience—but at a meaningful cost among women," Nataly Kelly, chief marketing officer at Zappi told me via email.

Although the ad may be resonating with men, appealing to a target audience is only one measure of an ad's success. Companies also have to consider how their advertising impacts their business partners and all of their customers.

Good Good Golf learned that lesson just last month. After releasing an ad depicting violence against a woman, retailers including Dick's Sporting Goods and Target pulled Good Good merchandise, and the company lost an opportunity to sponsor a PGA Tour and a reality show. Surveys also indicated that Good Good may have alienated their female customer base.

Novig may have also lost some potential female customers. "Every brand faces the same question with work like this: who are you willing to lose in order to win someone else? This ad moved men toward Novig and moved women who already bet online away from it, and women are now around 26% of that market," Kelly explained.

In addition, Novig also has partnerships that could face scrutiny. The New York Mets, an organization that has promoted girls and women in sports, are currently partnering with the company but did not respond to a request for comment about whether the Sweeney campaign would impact that relationship.

articles.title: ‘Some type of insecurity’: Shakur Stevenson talks falling out with Tank Davis
articles.summary: Shakur Stevenson says he’s going to continue to keep it classy with regards to Gervonta ‘Tank’ Davis.
articles.body:
In the midst of all the social media beef between fighters in the sport today, Shakur Stevenson spent a little time breaking down his ongoing beef with Tank Davis . While once on friendly terms, their relationship has soured over the years and while Shakur can't pin it down to any one particular thing, he does think Tank has some insecurities about him.

"There's so much that happened in that situation," Stevenson said of his falling out with Tank. "I don't know what it is with that dude, I don't know why is there like so much hatred upon me, but it is what it is. At the end of the day, look at this, if you ever look at me when I talk about him now — when I was younger I used to kind of be a little bit different, I used to be straight disrespectful — as I got older, more mature, I started learning how to speak in front of these cameras, learning how to talk.

"But, if you ever pay attention to me when I talk about him, I always say like he's a special fighter, he's a tremendous fighter. I try not to talk down on his name because I know that he's a good fighter, I give him his credit when it's due. But if you listen to him, he don't never say nothing good about me. He don't got nothing good to say about me. But I think it comes to like some type of insecurity.

"You know I'm the truth. Like, at the end of the day, you know I'm the truth, I know you the truth. So we the best of the best and I been saying it for years. So I'm going to keep it that way. I ain't going to lose my integrity. Hopefully he do his thing, I don't wish no ill upon him. Hopefully he come back and get all that other stuff situated."

At the moment Tank's boxing career has been in a medically induced coma with no definitive prognosis about an eventual return. That, however, hasn't prevented him from being a hot topic of conversation in the boxing world as he's still a huge money generator in the lower weight divisions, and therefore represents big paydays for potential foes.

articles.title: Celtics president Brad Stevens explains why he traded Jaylen Brown to a division rival
articles.summary: Boston Celtics GM Brad Stevens is ready to move forward from the Jaylen Brown trade, even after it encouraged LeBron James to join the 76ers.
articles.body:
BOSTON — Tuesday morning marked the start of a new chapter for the Boston Celtics , as they introduced veteran NBAers and first-year Green Teamers Paul George and Mike Conley Jr . to the media. Before this next phase could begin, though, Celtics President of Basketball Operations Brad Stevens had to close the book on the Jaylen Brown trade.

In early July, Stevens moved Brown in exchange for George, two first-round picks, and two second-round picks. This trade created a domino effect that ultimately encouraged future Hall of Famer LeBron James to team up with Brown and sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the 76ers . Stevens faced the media when Brown was initially dealt, yet he hadn't spoken to reporters since James went to Philly in late July.

When asked how he weighed trading Brown against the consequences of potentially strengthening a division rival, Stevens emphasized that the Celtics were moving on, regardless of the threat the Sixers might pose.

"Our focus is on us," he told Celtics Wire. "And obviously, we will look forward to any challenges. There are a lot of good teams all around the league, but we have to do what's best — what we think is in the best interest of us, both in the short and long term."

The two-time NBA Executive of the Year didn't elaborate on the "short and long term." He's largely covered that ground already. Losing Brown's contract opens things up financially in the years to come for the Celtics and allows them to afford some of their depth.

But, why did Stevens send Brown, the 2024 NBA Finals MVP, to an in-division rival? Stevens said himself in July that if he could have traded him to the Western Conference, he would have. The market for Brown may have collapsed, causing the C's to make a drastic deal before he was due a contract extension.

"So that was the decision, and we went through that in July," Stevens concluded.

Instead of dwelling on Brown, Stevens opted to focus on the future of the Celtics. He praised George, Conley Jr., and center Mitchell Robinson — who was planning to be at Tuesday's presser but had to cancel because of personal reasons — while sitting at the podium inside the Auerbach Center.

"Today is about Mike, Paul, and Mitch, who's not here, and making sure that we are ready to put our best foot forward," he said.

The excitement of a new season will help Stevens and company progress and forget about the trade saga. However, if the Celtics falter, or the Sixers thrive, escaping questions about Brown will prove difficult. That is where part of the gamble of this move becomes apparent.

To truly move forward, the Celtics need to advance in the standings, or at least sit close to the top seeds in the Eastern Conference. Dropping in the East rankings or failing to contend for a championship next season, regardless of the big picture the Celtics have planned internally, will bring backlash galore for the front office and have fans stuck in the past.

They may wonder "what if" rather than excitedly asking, "What's next?"

articles.title: Giants-Cowboys delivers 25.7 million viewers
articles.summary: The first Sunday of Week 1 ended with the latest installment of the Cowboys-Giants rivalry.
articles.body:
The first Sunday of Week 1 ended with the latest installment of the Cowboys-Giants rivalry. As expected, it drew a big crowd.

The game averaged 25.7 million viewers on NBC and Peacock. It made 2026 the first year since 2015 with both the kickoff game and the Week 1 Sunday night game at 25 million or more.

Viewership peaked at 29.0 million in the second quarter, from 9:00 to 9:15 p.m. ET.

It was also the most-watched Week 1 Sunday night game since 2015, when the Cowboys hosted the Giants. It was a four-percent bump over last year's Ravens-Bills classic, which Buffalo stormed back to win, 41-40.

articles.title: Gakpo the Standout as Liverpool Progress in the EFL Cup
articles.summary: Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham – EFL Cup Man of the MatchCody GakpoLiverpool FCCody Gakpo is starting to look like a completely different player under Andoni Iraola...
articles.body:
Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham – EFL Cup Man of the Match

Cody Gakpo is starting to look like a completely different player under Andoni Iraola .

The Dutch international was once again at the heart of everything good Liverpool produced against Tottenham, contributing to all three goals as the Reds secured a 3–1 victory at Anfield and progressed in the EFL Cup.

A hockey-type assist for the opening goal, a superb strike to double Liverpool's advantage and then an assist for the third made Gakpo the obvious choice for Man of the Match.

But the importance of his performance goes beyond the numbers.

There has been a noticeable change in Gakpo since Iraola arrived. The player who looked increasingly uncertain about his future on Merseyside during the summer is now beginning to look like somebody perfectly suited to the football this new Liverpool side is attempting to play.

The tempo is different. The movement is different. The intention is different.

Liverpool are playing faster and more directly, and that appears to suit Gakpo enormously.

The opening goal was a perfect example of Gakpo's contribution. He was involved in the move, carried the ball intelligently and helped create the opportunity before Liverpool eventually found the breakthrough.

Gakpo received the opportunity and made absolutely no mistake, producing a superb strike from the angle to put Liverpool two goals ahead.

His influence continued right until the closing stages, when he supplied the assist for Liverpool's third and effectively put the contest beyond Tottenham.

Two goal involvements in one night tell the story, but his general performance was just as encouraging.

Gakpo looked powerful, direct and confident. He was prepared to carry the ball, attack spaces and make things happen rather than simply waiting for the game to come to him.

That is precisely what Liverpool needs from him.

There is still plenty of work to do under Iraola, but Gakpo looks increasingly like one of the players who could benefit most from the change in approach.

Gakpo takes the award, but Giorgi Mamardashvili deserves a special mention.

The Georgian goalkeeper was superb in his shot-stopping and made several excellent saves to keep Liverpool ahead, including a brilliant low stop to his left after the interval and an extraordinary one-handed save later in the contest.

He probably would have been a serious contender for Man of the Match had it not been for the poor positioning that contributed to Tottenham's headed goal.

Even so, his overall performance was another positive.

Liverpool made numerous changes for this EFL Cup tie, brought several younger players into the starting XI and still produced a controlled 3–1 victory over Tottenham.

Alexis Mac Allister was very good, Trey Nyoni looked increasingly comfortable in the deeper midfield role and several of the younger players showed Iraola that they can contribute.

But on a night when Liverpool needed players to step forward, Gakpo was the man who consistently delivered.

The tide has certainly turned for the Dutchman.

A player who looked like he could leave Liverpool in the summer is now beginning to look like one of the most natural fits for Iraola's new football.

That can only be good news for Liverpool.

articles.title: Senate votes to move forward with Protect College Sports Act
articles.summary: The Senate on Tuesday voted to advance the Protect College Sports Act, an NCAA-backed, bipartisan bill aimed at setting federal guidelines for college sports amid a rapidly shifting landscape.
articles.body: The Senate on Tuesday voted to advance the Protect College Sports Act, an NCAA-backed, bipartisan bill aimed at setting federal guidelines for college sports amid a rapidly shifting landscape. The measure advanced on a 74-24 vote; it needed 60 votes to proceed. Timing on a vote for final passage in the Senate is unclear at the time. The legislation would still need to pass the House if it makes it through the Senate. The Protect College Sports Act is the latest attempt to set a national standard for the rules of college sports. In recent years, a variety of issues — ranging from eligibility to compensation — have been challenged in state courts. Decisions and temporary injunctions have quickly changed NCAA rules that had been in place for decades, paving the way for athletes to transfer schools freely or be compensated by their schools directly. The Protect College Sports Act aims to set a national standard regarding issues that include years of eligibility, how often players can transfer, compensation and more. The bill would also grant the NCAA an antitrust exemption and prevent future legal challenges over such rules. Professional leagues, such as the NFL and NBA, have antitrust exemptions. But athletes in those leagues collectively bargain over the rules. The legislation got support from both sides of the aisle after it was introduced by Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., earlier this year. The NCAA has lobbied Congress for years to pass a sweeping federal law after numerous state rulings have transformed the nature of college sports, particularly men’s and women’s basketball and football. “This bill might not be perfect, but it’s far, far away the best thing we got out there right now,” Gonzaga men’s basketball coach Mark Few said Monday alongside Cruz and Cantwell. The Protect College Sports Act also has numerous critics, including the Congressional Black Caucus and the NAACP. One of its most outspoken critics has been Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn. “This bill protects the billions of dollars that coaches and sports industry executives are making over the suppression of compensation for some of the most highly valued athletes in the world,” Murphy told reporters Monday. “What we’re being asked to do is to basically allow colleges and conferences and the NCAA to illegally collude.” Proponents and detractors of the legislation have been jockeying for position publicly. Cruz recently appeared on ESPN’s “College GameDay,” a popular college football pregame show, to stump for the measure. Murphy offered a rebuttal on Stephen A. Smith’s “Straight Shooter” podcast. Meanwhile, advocates for athletes have pointed to other issues with the bill, including how it could potentially create a loophole for schools to escape accountability for a variety of violations, including sexual abuse.

articles.title: Bucs’ Contract Decision Gets Clearer After Week 1
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough decision to make when it comes to veteran defender Yaya Diaby. He is entering the last year of his rookie salary contra...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough decision to make when it comes to veteran defender Yaya Diaby . He is entering the last year of his rookie salary contract, and right now the team is letting things play out as they decide whether to offer him an extension to stay with the team or let him leave in free agency.

Scott Reynolds of Pewter Report noted that if his Week 1 performance is any indication of what the Bucs are going to get from Diaby in 2026, they are likely to let another team pay him in free agency.

"He's got to put up some statistics; he's got to prove he can get to the quarterback," said Reynolds on the Pewter Report podcast. "If he has any more of these types of games, some team will pay him…there will be a team that will overpay Yaya Diaby, but if he keeps playing like this, hopefully it's not the Tampa Bay Buccaneers."

Diaby played 40 snaps for the Bucs and had 24 pass rush snaps. He recorded just one pressure. Overall, he had a pass rush grade of 51.5, which is below average. Last year, Diaby only had one game worse than his performance in Week 1, according to PFF.

The Bucs edge rusher is going to have to rebound quickly.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers Might Not Extend Veteran Yaya Diaby

Diaby has been hot and cold for the Buccaneers since entering the NFL , which is why he has not received a contract extension yet. The third-round pick hit the ground running in his rookie season. He recorded 7.5 sacks and only started about halfway through the year.

However, in his second season, he dropped to 4.5 sacks. Things picked up in year three. Still, he put up seven sacks, which is right below his rookie season. He has been unable to produce more than he did in his first year with the Bucs.

As Reynolds points out, young edge rushers with any hint of production get overpaid. He pointed to Jaelan Phillips on his podcast. He averages seven sacks per season and has a history of injuries. Still, the Panthers wound up paying him $30M per year in free agency.

The Bucs will see his inconsistency and not want to pay him. Diaby will see the big money in free agency and not want to settle with Tampa Bay.

The Bucs have had a lot of tough decisions to make when it comes to the future of their franchise. They just gave big extensions to quarterback Baker Mayfield and defensive tackle Vita Vea.

Not only is Diaby a situation where he is looking to cash in, but the Bucs are also debating guard Cody Mauch and how much he will demand on the open market. As both get closer to free agency, it will be harder to retain them.

Still, this season will determine how much both can command on the open market.

articles.title: Connor Bedard named 37th Blackhawks captain in team history
articles.summary: CHICAGO — In the United Center’s atrium, star center Connor Bedard entered the stage with Chicago Blackhawks CEO and Chairman Danny Wirtz, general manager Ky...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — In the United Center's atrium, star center Connor Bedard entered the stage with Chicago Blackhawks CEO and Chairman Danny Wirtz, general manager Kyle Davidson and coach Jeff Blashill. The quartet posed in front of the camera with Bedard's new jersey.

The number's still 98, and there's still a patch near the shoulder. This time, the letter is a little more significant.

"The 'C' on someone is not something we take for granted at all, but Connor's someone we feel is uniquely qualified to wear the 'C,' " Davidson said. "He's someone who's occupied a unique and rare position in his hockey career, even before his time in Chicago.

"He's a natural-born leader, someone we're consistently impressed by (with his) commitment to winning on the ice and high standards. He loves the game, loves the city, wants to be leader of the group and we know he'll continue to strive to raise the bar."

The Chicago Blackhawks formally announced at a news conference on Tuesday afternoon that the No. 1 pick in the 2023 NHL draft will be the team's 37th captain.

"Being named captain of the Blackhawks is an unbelievable honor and something I'm truly humbled by. The captains who have come before me have left an incredible legacy," Bedard said in a statement. "To now have the opportunity to carry that tradition forward is something I don't take lightly. I'm grateful to the organization and my teammates for putting their trust in me to lead this team. We're building something really special here, and I'm committed to making the entire Blackhawks organization and our fans proud."

With the "C" patch bestowed, the 21-year-old becomes the NHL's youngest captain. He trails only Jonathan Toews in the Hawks' record books, as the retired franchise legend was named captain at 20 years and 79 days old.

"One of the biggest honors in my life, and for a storied franchise like this to be named captain and follow in the footsteps of (Nick) Foligno, (Chris Chelios), Toews, you can go down the list," Bedard said on Tuesday. "I hope we can really do some great things here in the next little while."

Toews led the Hawks as team captain for 14 seasons, winning three Stanley Cups along the way. To this day, it remains the longest "C" patch tenure in franchise history.

Bedard is expected to hold the patch for a long time. It's an honor and a responsibility, and the 21-year-old will be patient with himself as time moves on.

"Every new experience is something you have to learn, (but) I feel ready," Bedard said. "The last three years, you grow a lot and become more used to the day-to-day life and your teammates and just how close our group is, (that) really helps.

"It's really a family and everyone can talk to each other and give each other advice, whatever you need. That part makes it easy for us. I'm excited to ask other guys' questions and be led by them as well."

Bedard isn't expected to make his season debut until November after undergoing offseason shoulder surgery in July.

But Tuesday's announcement confirms the widely anticipated move for Bedard, who was presumed captain ever since Foligno was traded to the Minnesota Wild last season. Bedard never claimed the title for himself, but noted that he would be grateful for the recognition.

"If I did get the 'C', I'm not going to change who I am and become something different just because of that letter," Bedard said in April. "It's an added responsibility that I do think I'd be ready for — a lot of guys could be ready for it in that room — but it would be a special honor."

The forward had a brief experience with the alternate captain's patch last season on Nov. 19 against the Calgary Flames . With Foligno and Jason Dickinson on injury reserve, Bedard scored his second career hat trick to lift the Hawks to a 5-2 win.

"I've been so fortunate to learn from guys like (Foligno), (Dickinson), ( Connor Murphy ) — all those guys that have been leaders in our room," Bedard said then. "The Blackhawks jersey in general is such a special thing. There have been a lot of great players who have a letter on their chest, and it's a great honor and something I don't take lightly."

On March 3, Hawks coach Jeff Blashill — who is now entering his second season — awarded Bedard with the "A" for the remainder of the season.

"I had given it to him earlier in the year when we had injury issues," Blashill said. "I think he's earned it with his commitment to winning hockey."

Bedard signed a five-year, $75 million contract in July, and stated later that he dismissed offer sheets from other teams.

"For me, I kind of let them know from the start that it wasn't something I was ever going to do," Bedard said on the Overdrive podcast on July 24. "The risk of not being a Blackhawk wasn't worth any amount of money."

Now, when he returns, he will lead a new-look Hawks team in hopes of a playoff berth. New additions include forwards Patrick Kane and Cole Smith , and defensemen Bowen Byram and Ian Cole .

Oliver Moore , Tyler Bertuzzi and Kane were front row for Bedard's captaincy announcement. After poking fun at the 37-year-old, Bedard gushed at the chance to take the ice with Kane.

"When we talk about leadership, everything we dream of and want to accomplish as a team, we watched him," Bedard said of Kane. "He's still one of the best players in the league and that's just going to add so much."

Blashill also announced that Bertuzzi and Kane will round out the leadership group as the alternate captains.

"It's a fun group, a happy group, there's good vibes and these guys want to be good players," Kane said. "It's pushing me in a way, too — you're 37, turning 38, and accomplish some great things, but it still feels like there's a lot left on the table and a lot more you want to accomplish because these guys haven't done it and they're pushing to do it."

The Milwaukee Brewers are riding high as one of MLB's top teams. Their 93-57 record is the best in the league, and they'll have a chance to prove they belong with a new series against the Pittsburgh Pirates on deck. Amid this new series, a decision has been announced regarding Cooper Pratt.

Both teams have announced their probable starters, with Jacob Misiorowski taking the mound for the Brewers as Lake Bachar starts for the Pirates. Tuesday night's game will begin at 4:40 PM Mountain Time, 6:40 PM Eastern Time.

Milwaukee Brewers News: Cooper Pratt Out, David Hamilton In

"Brewers 9/15: G. Mitchell CF, J. Chourio LF, B. Turang 2B, W. Contreras C, J. Bauers 1B, C. Yelich DH, L. Lara RF. J. Ortiz SS, D. Hamilton 3B, J. Misiorowski SP," the Underdog MLB account shared on social media prior to the September 15th match.

Looking at Cooper Pratt & David Hamilton

Hamilton, meanwhile, has produced 76 hits, 11 doubles, three triples, four home runs, 25 RBIs, and 27 stolen bases in 112 games. Unlike Pratt, Hamilton brings some versatility with the positions that he plays.

During the 2026 season, Hamilton has started 13 games at second base, 79 at third base, and 33 at shortstop. For Tuesday night's game, he will play third base while Joey Ortiz slides over to cover shortstop for the removed Pratt.

We are three weeks removed from when Pratt was benched during a series against the New York Mets .

Since then, Pratt has been a steady member of the Brewers lineup. However, with a long season nearing its end, it doesn't hurt to give players an extra day of rest here and there.

articles.title: Sidney Crosby Talks Next Penguins Contract, Retirement Buzz Ahead of 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: Sidney Crosby is currently set to play the 2026-27 season on an expiring contract as retirement rumors run rampant, but the Pittsburgh Penguins legend isn't sweating about striking a new deal before the campaign starts.
articles.body:
Sidney Crosby is currently set to play the 2026-27 season on an expiring contract as retirement rumors run rampant, but the Pittsburgh Penguins legend isn't sweating about striking a new deal before the campaign starts.

Crosby said he'll let president of hockey operations/general manager Kyle Dubas and his agent, Pat Brisson, figure out the details of his next deal.

"I don't know," Crosby told The Athletic's Josh Yohe . "I'm going to let Pat and Kyle figure that out. I wouldn't say there's a hard timeline. It's something that I'll let them discuss. At this point in my career, it's hard to project how long I'll play for. We'll see what happens."

Capitals Say Alex Ovechkin Was Asked to Film United Russia Ad While Home This Summer (AP)

As for his retirement, Crosby gave no indication of when he'll hang it up, but said he'll know when it's time.

"I think it's a combination of everything," he said. "You talk to guys who are later in their careers, and I think it's different for everyone. I don't think you ever know until you get to that point. I'm guessing it's your level (of play), how your body feels, a combination of things."

Despite being 39 years old, Crosby had a productive 2025-26 season, recording 29 goals and 45 assists while playing 68 games. He helped lead the Penguins to the playoffs for the first time since 2022.

He dealt with some knee injuries throughout last season but was overall able to stay healthy.

"Overall, I feel pretty good," he said. "I'm hoping it's not something I'll have to think about too much. That's (age) just the reality of things. I'm happy with how I feel. We'll just go from there."

A player of Crosby's age can't avoid retirement rumors, but he's clearly taking it one day at a time as he weighs his future.

articles.title: Kenny Dillingham Reveals Arizona State’s Biggest Challenge Adjusting to London
articles.summary: The Arizona State Sun Devils are heading into a crucial week three contest against the Kansas Jayhawks. Not only is Arizona State coming off of a loss to Tex...
articles.body:
The Arizona State Sun Devils are heading into a crucial week three contest against the Kansas Jayhawks.

Not only is Arizona State coming off of a loss to Texas A&M, they are also facing a duo of week three challenges. These challenges are opening up Big 12 play against Kansas, as well as playing in London, England.

Head coach Kenny Dillingham is well aware of these challenges, speaking about them following Tuesday's practice.

Arizona State's Challenges in London are Apparent

Dillingham recognizes the upside in playing overseas is next to zero. He still acknowledges that this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for his team.

"Zero positives from a football perspective. The positive is our kids get an experience that I wasn't gonna rob them from."

The Sun Devils had no choice but to fly directly to London following the Texas A&M battle. Kansas, on the other hand, is traveling to London mid-week. Whether this is an advantage one way or the other is a mystery, but Dillingham didn't get any sleep for the first 36 hours in London.

There is still upside to this trip – even through the challenges. One of the breaks is taking advantage of the much cooler weather in London, while also taking advantage of playing a top-10 team. Kansas did take on ranked Missouri last week, but the Aggies are seemingly a step above as an overall team.

What Sun Devils can Take Into Kansas Matchup

There were several aspects of Arizona State's performance against Texas A&M that seem to be sustainable.

Among them is the role QB Cutter Boley plays in the offense. The Kentucky native is putting together a nice start behind confident delivery, distributing the ball evenly, and extending plays when necessary.

Reed Harris and Omarion Miller are particular beneficiaries of Boley's strong start. The two receivers are an inherent mismatch against a Kansas secondary that was seemingly overwhelmed by Missouri.

Dillingham's play-calling is an absolute advantage heading into the game as well. Arizona State's rushing attack is promising, but game flow prevented others outside of Kyson Brown from making a mark. The ability to utilize various personnel packages built around different running backs allows for Boley to dictate the game out of play action, as well as in shorter yardage situations.

The offensive line is in for a challenge this week as well, but the group is in a decent position. Guard Wade Helton is out for a few weeks, but reserve Rob Lapuaho is taking his place, and the growth he is showing under OL coach Saga Tuitele is promising.

There are many things that the Arizona State coaching staff can take from the last few weeks. This includes many points of attack that the group can throw at Kansas, as well as how to manage a victory.

articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox are coming off back-to-back wins to take a three-game series from the Kansas City Royals .

After a day-off Monday, the Red Sox are now in Texas to take on the Rangers, a team just one game out of the lead in its division, the American League West.

Before taking on the Rangers, the Red Sox announced a lineup move with their young star Roman Anthony .

The 22-year-old Anthony is back in left field, not the less stressful designated hitter spot, when the Red Sox open their series against the Rangers at Globe Life Field. Mickey Gasper slides into the DH spot instead, with Jarren Duran in center, confirmed by Boston Globe Red Sox reporter Tim Healey ahead of Tuesday's lineup card.

The alignment has become the season's rhythm. Anthony has DH'd 21 times, played left field 20 times and logged three appearances in right through the first 44 games he has played in this injury-interrupted season, a split Boston has leaned on since he returned from a three-month absence with a right hand injury. Masataka Yoshida remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, which opens the DH chair for Gasper, a versatile bat hitting .265/.373/.488 with nine home runs in 57 games this season who has also filled in at first base and catcher when needed.

SP: Patrick Sandoval (LHP) • 1-5, 4.58 ERA

September 15, 2026 • Globe Life Field, Arlington, TX • 8:05 PM ET • Red Sox at Rangers

Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG). Umpire: Ben May • Weather: 98°, Wind 11 mph • O/U: 8 Runs • Line: BOS +109 / TEX -131.

The sample stays small, and the metrics are mixed rather than glowing. Anthony has racked up five Defensive Runs Saved in left field this year, according to FanGraphs' left field fielding metrics , a number that looks sharp until it's stacked against two errors on 33 total chances there. Statcast tells a cooler story. Anthony sits at minus-1 Outs Above Average in left through 30 tracked attempts, converting 83% of them against an 85% expected success rate, according to Statcast's outs above average tracking . Baseball-Reference lands in between, crediting him a .939 fielding percentage in left and five defensive runs above average over 160.1 innings, according to Baseball-Reference's total zone fielding data . None of it makes Anthony a defensive liability. It also doesn't make him a plus glove — an average left fielder still learning the position, arm and range included.

Roman Anthony's Bat Away From Designated Hitter

At the plate, Anthony has cooled from the .292 average and .859 OPS that made him last year's runner-up for AL Rookie of the Year. His 2026 line sits at .241/.342/.376 with four home runs, and his expected weighted on-base average of .349 outpaces his actual mark of .321, a gap tied largely to a hard-hit rate that's dropped from 60.3% a year ago to 48.7% now. He went just 6-for-13 over his last three games against Kansas City, connecting on a go-ahead single Sunday, according to Reuters.

Splitting his production by role tells a real, if modest, story. Playing the outfield this year, Anthony has hit .241 with a .351 on-base percentage but just a .265 slugging mark, according to CBS Sports' role-based batting splits .

As the DH, his average dips to .233, but his slugging jumps to .442, with more of his extra-base pop showing up when hitting is his only job. Splits tracked by FanGraphs' position-based batting split data echo the pattern of steadier on-base skills in left field, more thump at DH. There's no obvious drag on his batting average. But his power shows up more when he doesn't play the outfield.

None of this settles the long-term question of where Anthony ultimately fits best. The sample from this injury-shortened season remains too thin to draw firm conclusions about his defensive ceiling or whether the DH-outfield rotation helps or hurts his overall production. For now, the Red Sox keep threading the needle, running him out in left against the Rangers and trusting the bat to show up wherever he stands.

articles.summary: Acrobatic and tumbling programs typically carry 35 to 45 student-athletes, according to Siena, one of many schools grappling with enrollment issues. Siena's...
articles.body:
Siena University athletic director John D'Argenio is leading a search for a coach for a new sport at his school.

Siena is adding women's acrobatics and tumbling as its 22nd NCAA Division I sport, starting with the 2027-28 academic year.

D'Argenio said Tuesday he already received applications from coaching candidates, one day after Siena made the announcement.

"We have a few in, so we'll start ASAP, trying to identify some candidates and interview people," D'Argenio said. "Ideally, we'd love to have somebody in the next couple of months, so they can start recruiting for next year."

Siena becomes the 54th collegiate institution to sponsor acrobatics and tumbling as a varsity sport. Athletes perform a series of synchronized skills in events such as acrobatics, pyramid, toss, tumbling and team routines in front of judges.

Competing during the spring, Siena's acrobatics and tumbling team will hold its home contests at UHY Center, also the school's venue for women's basketball and volleyball. The Saints will compete in six to 12 meets in matchups of two or three teams.

Acrobatic and tumbling programs typically carry 35 to 45 student-athletes, according to Siena, one of many schools grappling with enrollment issues. Siena's enrollment dropped more than 9% last year.

"I think it's very important ... to help contribute to the overall enrollment," D'Argenio said. "I think we do a reasonably good job now, but if we can find ways to add incremental students and give them a good athletic experience, I think that's really important."

The NCAA will hold its first championships for acrobatics and tumbling from April 22 to 25, 2027.

"Our focus is on strategic growth that delivers real value for students," said Siena president Chuck Seifert in a news release. "Acrobatics & tumbling expands opportunity, enhances the student experience, and positions Siena to compete nationally as the sport enters NCAA championship status."

It's the first sport Siena is adding since men's and women's indoor and outdoor track in 2015-16.

D'Argenio said Siena will offer some partial athletic scholarships for acrobatics and tumbling. Siena will determine the amount after comparing with other schools.

Siena becomes the sixth Metro Conference school to start acrobatics and tumbling, joining Canisius, Iona, Manhattan, Quinnipiac, and Sacred Heart.

"Along with the enrollment piece, what we've seen is it's become more and more popular across the country," D'Argenio said. "It's an emerging sport for women in the NCAA. … The NCAA will host a championship, and from an athletics standpoint, that was attractive. And then I also think from a recruitment standpoint, not just more students, but they come from different parts of the country or the region that we might normally recruit students from."

While Siena will have to buy mats and other equipment, D'Argenio said, acrobatics and tumbling doesn't require another facility or retrofitting UHY Center. The school can also use other parts of the Marcelle Athletic Complex for practices, he said.

D'Argenio said he's spoken to officials from other schools, including Canisius and Iona. The Golden Griffins went 4-3 in their inaugural season last year. Iona, which added the sport in 2024, went 3-4 last season.

The National Collegiate Acrobatics & Tumbling Association (NCATA) currently governs the sport and draws its athletes from gymnastics, cheerleading, diving, dance, and other strength-based sports, according to Siena.

D'Argenio said he will hire a full-time head coach and a part-time assistant.

"It's somewhat like recruiting for any coach, right?" D'Argenio said. "You try to identify somebody that can have good relationships with their players and understand the values of Siena."

articles.title: Nashville Predators share updated Bridgestone Arena, Centennial Ice Rink renderings
articles.summary: New renderings of Bridgestone Arena show the build-out of Broadway, including food and retail, improved access and new design elements.
articles.body:
The Nashville Predators released new renderings Sept. 15 of upcoming upgrades for Bridgestone Arena and Centennial Ice Rink .

The arena upgrades show the build-out for the 5th Avenue and Broadway side of the building, which includes additional access in and out, more retail and food options, and new design elements to the spire and exterior wall.

Construction on this project, which is called "Smashville's Next Stage," is expected to begin in summer 2027 and be completed within three years.

Bridgestone Arena, Centennial Ice Rink renderings, Nashville Predators

The team also released never-seen-before images of upgrades to the Predators ' training facilities at Centennial Ice Rink. The images show a new rear entrance to the building (replacing the current players-only parking lot area), a players lounge and recovery room, and a dining area.

This project is the next step in the Predators' capital commitment to the facility, which is part of the Centennial Sportsplex. In January, the Predators finalized a lease agreement with Metro Nashville to commit up to $30 million in capital upgrades in exchange for operational control of the ice facilities.

The upgrades released in these renderings are not a part of that $30 million figure, but instead an additional expense by the team to upgrade the team's locker room facilities at Centennial.

These upgrades are expected to be completed by September 2027.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Pumps Brakes on Blockbuster Lions Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Dan Campbell downplayed expectations of a blockbuster Lions trade despite Detroit creating roughly $35.7 million in new salary-cap space.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions suddenly have enough salary-cap room to make people dream big.

Dan Campbell is suggesting everyone might want to slow down a little.

Detroit recently restructured the contracts of Penei Sewell and Amon-Ra St. Brown , creating approximately $35.7 million in additional 2026 cap space and pushing the Lions to roughly $38 million in available room. The moves immediately sparked speculation that Brad Holmes could be positioning Detroit for a major in-season acquisition.

Campbell was asked Tuesday whether that flexibility could lead to the Lions taking a significant swing on the trade market.

His answer was not exactly gasoline for the rumor mill.

"I don't see that," Campbell said . "I would say this, though. It gives us options. Whether that be our own guys or… it just gives us flexibility here before the season starts because there's a lot that can happen."

There is plenty packed into that answer.

Just probably not the blockbuster announcement some Lions fans were hoping to hear.

Lions Created Flexibility, Not Necessarily a Trade Fund

Detroit did not merely scrape together a few million dollars. The Lions created one of the largest pools of available cap space in the NFL almost overnight. As we explained when Detroit reworked the Sewell and St. Brown contracts , the maneuver gave Holmes substantially more freedom to react during the season.

Detroit could absorb the contract of a player acquired before the trade deadline. It could help facilitate extensions for members of its own young core. The Lions can also carry unused cap room into 2027 rather than spending simply because the money exists.

Campbell's answer sounded much more like the latter philosophy.

Do not manufacture a reason to use them.

What Does Campbell's Comment Mean for Joey Porter Jr.?

Naturally, this conversation lands on Joey Porter Jr.

The Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback has been connected to Detroit as his contract situation remains unresolved, and reports have indicated the Steelers are willing to listen to trade offers. Detroit's need at corner also became harder to ignore after the Lions allowed 410 passing yards in their Week 1 victory over New Orleans .

Long before the latest trade chatter picked up, we examined a hypothetical deal that would send Porter to Detroit for a first-round pick . At that point, it was strictly a proposed trade, not evidence the Lions were pursuing him.

The situation has become more interesting since then, but Campbell's comments are a useful reminder not to skip several steps.

He was not specifically asked about Porter, and he could not publicly negotiate another team's player anyway. His response does not prove Detroit has no interest.

It does, however, make one thing clear: the Lions did not create all this cap room simply because a blockbuster deal is waiting to be announced.

Nothing about Campbell's answer means Holmes will ignore the trade market.

Detroit considers itself a contender, and contenders should be willing to improve when the right opportunity presents itself. If an impact corner, pass rusher or another player at a position of need becomes available at a price Holmes considers reasonable, Detroit now has the financial flexibility to act quickly.

The key words are right opportunity and reasonable price.

Holmes has built the current roster largely by drafting, developing and retaining players rather than treating every offseason or trade deadline like fantasy football. Campbell's comments suggest that philosophy has not suddenly changed because the Lions found an extra $35 million on their cap sheet.

Feeling obligated to spend it would not be.

So, yes, Detroit now has the money to make a major move.

Campbell just made it clear that having the ability to swing for the fences and actually deciding to do it are two very different things.

articles.title: Todd Monken pushes back on Mike Tomlin’s assessment: ‘That’s not Browns being Browns’
articles.summary: Pretty much every NFL fan who watched the Cleveland Browns’ moribund performance in Week 1 of the NFL season last weekend thought to themselves something aki...
articles.body:
Pretty much every NFL fan who watched the Cleveland Browns ' moribund performance in Week 1 of the NFL season last weekend thought to themselves something akin to, "that's the Browns for you."

That includes NBC's Mike Tomlin , who, when describing quarterback Deshaun Watson 's miserable performance in a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , said, "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster , the Browns is the Browns."

The zinger landed extra hard given that Tomlin coached one of the Browns' biggest rivals for 19 seasons, going 28-10-1 against Cleveland in that time.

Browns first-year coach Todd Monken was asked about Tomlin's comments during his Monday video press conference , and he seemed understandably perturbed by them.

"Well, again, everybody's afforded their opinions. That's what you do when you go from coaching to television," Monken said. "We have to own that. We have to own that. We didn't play very well. I don't see it that way, Browns being Browns. I don't see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn't play well. That's one week. That's not Browns being Browns, that's Browns being poorly on one week.

"So, again, everybody's afforded their opinion. And the only way to change people's opinion is to play better. That's a fact. We don't want to be considered an also-ran, then we have to play better. We have to coach better, and we have to play better."

Monken is technically correct, but this is the Browns we're talking about . There's a reason a lot of people were nodding their heads when they heard Tomlin say it.

articles.title: Washington Football Freshman WR Duo Excels Vs. Utah State
articles.summary: Two Washington Huskies freshmen wide receivers got their first extended taste of college football in Saturday's 16-14 win over Utah State.
articles.body:
In a world of few bright spots offensively, two Washington Huskies freshmen wide receivers played key roles in Saturday's 16-14 win over Utah State.

Jordan Clay, a 6-foot-3, 210-pound San Antonio, Texas, native, became an early next-man-up target for third-year quarterback Demond Williams Jr. after veteran Christian Moss was unable to suit up after he suffered an injury against Washington State.

The one-time Baylor commit hauled in consecutive 8-yard receptions for his first two catches as a Husky on the final play of the first quarter and the first play of the second quarter. Clay then hauled in a crucial 19-yard contested catch with 10 minutes, which set up UW's first touchdown to retake the lead at 10-7.

"Jordan Clay has shown us his ability to win one-on-one battles," Jedd Fisch said on Monday. "The circus route that he caught on the sideline with a (holding call) as well was extremely impressive. It showed his ball skills. I mean, he's got 10-and-a-half (inch) hands. He's got huge hands. So you can see his ability to make those plucks in the air."

It proved to be the last throw Williams Jr. made on the drive as freshman running back Ansu Sanoe and veteran Trey Cooley, along with the third-year passer, finished off the drive with six consecutive runs to cap off he drive.

Fisch said Clay and fellow first-year receiver Trez Davis—who vaulted into a bigger role than expected against the Aggies when fourth-year starter Rashid Williams left the game in the first half due to injury—showed poise in the narrow victory this past weekend.

Clay finished the game with four catches for 42 yards while Davis added four catches for 44 yards behind second-year starter Dezmen Roebuck. Much of Davis' production came on the final drive of the first half, a 19-yard reception in front of Roebuck going towards the Huskies ' sideline, and then a 7-yard catch to set up a 48-yard field goal by Tyler Robles.

"We were expecting Jordan to play a significant amount this week," Fisch said. "Trez, we were still kind of working into the rotation, and then Rashid went down early. I thought that Trez had incredible poise. The scramble play that he caught on the sideline with (Dezmen Roebuck) almost coming in front of him, to have the temperament to make that catch (was impressive)."

Fisch noted that Davis' second catch just before the end of the first half hadn't been practiced. Davis made it happen in three seconds despite the ensuing field goal attempt going wide right to keep the score at 10-7.

With Moss expected to be out until at least the start of November and Rashid Williams week-to-week, on top of Fisch's insistence to play freshmen and young players early and often, could mean the first-year UW receiver duo are set to join Roebuck and second-year pass catcher Chris Lawson as the main targets for Williams Jr. as the 2026 season moves along.

"They're both good-sized wideouts, and they're both super young," Fisch said. "But they both have a ton of upside."

articles.title: Bengals’ fast start should show up in power rankings…right?
articles.summary: Is the big start for the Bengals enough to get some power rankings respect?
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals did the one thing everyone agrees they must do: Start fast.

Said fast start included a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 1. That box score is a bit of a lie, too, because the Bengals effectively dominated most of the game, only for one Joe Burrow mistake to gift the Bucs a score.

So, a solid offensive showing and a competent defense that only surrendered 20 points and forced four turnovers.

That means a big jump in the power rankings for the Bengals, right?

At USA Today, Nate Davis bumps the Bengals up one spot to No. 9, writing that "Sunday's defensive effort should sow hope for the Stripes amid their modest offensive debut."

Over at Sports Illustrated, Conor Orr puts the Bengals 13th overall: "Lawrence was one of the best defensive tackles in true pass rush sets throughout the entire weekend. A major upgrade for Cincinnati."

And at ESPN , it's another one-spot jump up to No .15 for the Bengals. The writeup notes that Boye Mafe led all Bengals linemen with 37 snaps, matching rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell with four pressures to go with his sack, forced fumble and fumble recovery.

No top 10 for the Bengals just yet at Yahoo Sports, either. Frank Schwab has them at No. 12.

"Turnovers aren't guaranteed to carry over week to week but the Bengals forced four, including one that was returned for a touchdown," Schwab wrote. "Cincinnati isn't going to be great on defense, but there have been some good teams to live off having a great offense and a defense that takes chances and makes a few game-changing plays. Maybe the Bengals can be that type of defense. That would be enough."

It's a two-spot jump up to No. 14 for the Bengals at The Athletic, with Chad Graff and Josh Kendall also happy to see Burrow get a defense that can help him out: "The bar might have been on the floor for that side of the ball after last season, but the new-look Cincinnati defense came to play against Tampa Bay , forcing four turnovers and notching four sacks. It was an especially impressive win considering Ja'Marr Chase caught only two passes for 12 yards."
