articles.title: Lions Week 2 Plans for Jahmyr Gibbs’ Workload Revealed
articles.summary: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 34 touches in the team’s Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints. While that seemed unprecedented fo...
articles.body:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 34 touches in the team's Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints . While that seemed unprecedented for the star runner who signed a three-year, $67.75M extension this offseason, reports are that the team plans to give him a similar workload in Week 2 at the Buffalo Bills .

Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reported from Lions practice, and he noted that the sentiment is clear: the Lions are not worried about the workload for Gibbs.

"From what I'm hearing, he's going to get close to that Thursday," said Wolfe on the potential of matching his career-high in touches for the second straight week. "Short week, no worries for them."

Wolfe added that Gibbs is on a mission to prove that his size does not mean that he is a small back. Gibbs told Wolfe that he has run between the tackles his entire career, and he can handle the power, along with the speed of being a running back.

Head coach Dan Campbell had two words of advice for Gibbs when it comes to his potential workload on such a short week: ' drink Gatorade '

Detroit Lions Plan to Feed Jahmyr Gibbs in Week 2

The reality is that as things stand, the Lions do not have any other option but to feed Gibbs. They traded his backup, David Montgomery , this offseason and did not do well enough when it comes to replacing him.

Isiah Pacheco was expected to be the backup. However, he fractured his leg in 2024 and was not the same back in 2025. He was not nearly as healthy, either.

Pacheco came into Lions camp and immediately got banged up. As he tried to return, he suffered a new injury. The team put him on the IR, and Wolfe reported that they expect him to be out until December.

Sione Vaki assumed the role as backup. However, he is a former safety who has hardly seen the field on offense. That showed in Week 1, as he struggled.

They also have Jacob Saylors , but the former UDFA has more work in the UFL than the NFL.

All of this indicates Gibbs will continue to get work.

Gibbs was excellent in his first game as the bell cow runner. He had 29 rushes for 156 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. More importantly, he had a 62% success rate as a runner. It was the second-most yards of his career and the most carries.

He also added five catches for 30 yards in the passing game.

At his current pace, he would be touching the football 578 times. The single-season record for touches in a season is 492. Gibbs will not be playing in tight overtime games all season.

However, the team will have to find ways to cut into his current workload. It can work in the short-term, but he cannot hold up if he gets this type of work every week.

articles.title: ‘He Seems Fed Up’ — Super Bowl Champion Reacts to Aaron Rodgers’ Bizarre Shailene Woodley Confession
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers recently peeled back the curtain on his breakup with actress Shailene Woodley and, after hearing the details, Super Bowl champion Leonard Fourn...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers recently peeled back the curtain on his breakup with actress Shailene Woodley and, after hearing the details, Super Bowl champion Leonard Fournette came away with a much simpler read on the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback.

The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back reacted to Rodgers' recent account of his failed engagement to Woodley, focusing on how willing Rodgers suddenly seems to discuss a relationship he had largely kept private for years.

Leonard Fournette Reacts to Aaron Rodgers' Shailene Woodley Story

Rodgers discussed Woodley during an appearance on Cam Heyward 's "Not Just Football" podcast. He claimed that only days after she accepted his marriage proposal, Woodley told him she wanted to sleep with another man before they got married.

Woodley has not publicly confirmed or denied Rodgers' version of that private conversation. During a pre-Emmy awards event, Woodley laughed and walked away when a reporter asked about Rodgers, but she did not address his specific allegation.

Fournette reacted to the story on his podcast " 4th and South" and sounded stunned that Rodgers was sharing that level of detail publicly.

The conversation quickly shifted from the particulars of Rodgers' allegation to what his willingness to discuss it suggested about his mindset. Fournette said Rodgers appeared to be "taking the gloves off" and wondered whether he had been holding frustration in for years before deciding to air it publicly.

Fournette also made clear that, in his view, the alleged request would have ended the relationship immediately.

"Would you still kind of go through with the marriage, though?" his co-host Jarvis Landry asked.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"What? [expletive] no," Fournette responded.

Rodgers' original breakup comments have already produced several rounds of reaction. He insisted during the interview that public narratives about the breakup did not accurately reflect what happened between them.

Rodgers Opens 22nd NFL Season With Win Over Falcons

The timing has made the story even more unusual. Rodgers is still Pittsburgh 's starting quarterback at 42 and opened his 22nd NFL season by completing 24-of-40 passes for 221 yards, 1 touchdown, and no interceptions in the Steelers' 20-13 win over Atlanta.

His recent football performance has not matched his peak years. In Week 1, Rodgers' 67.9 QB Impact Score ranked 29th among all qualifying quarterbacks (which mirrored his 29th ranking in 2025).

That has little to do with what happened between Rodgers and Woodley, but it does underline how unusual this stage of his career has become.

Rodgers is simultaneously trying to lead a playoff contender and publicly revisiting personal relationships that ended years ago.

Fournette's reaction captured the surprise surrounding that shift. Rodgers has often criticized speculation about his private life, yet his latest podcast appearance offered some of the most personal details he has ever shared.

Whether Woodley eventually offers a different account remains to be seen. From Fournette's perspective, though, Rodgers did not sound interested in keeping much bottled up anymore.

articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani hit off a tee on Sept. 15, and while Dave Roberts didn't commit to a timeline, he's confident Ohtani can return before the playoffs.
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani has taken his first steps to returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup.

Though he's not currently with the team for their three-game series in Cincinnati , Ohtani began his hitting progression in LA and "felt good" after hitting off a tee, manager Dave Roberts told reporters before the Dodgers played the Reds on Tuesday, Sept. 15 .

"I don't know what's in store for tomorrow, but I know there's gonna be a consistent build up," Roberts told reporters. "Don't know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive. Hopefully we can keep building towards that."

It was the first time Ohtani swung a bat since landing on the 15-day injured list after nagging injuries in his left knee and right bicep have led to a prolonged slump at the plate for the back-to-back National League MVP. He's already ruled out the possibility of returning to the mound as a pitcher this season, opting instead to focus solely on being a hitter for the rest of 2026.

The soonest Ohtani could see a return to action would be the final series of the regular season against the San Francisco Giants starting on Sept. 25, and though Roberts was noncommittal on a firm timeline, he expressed hope that Ohtani could be back in the lineup at some point before the postseason.

"Whether it happens or not is to be determined," Roberts said. "But I do expect him to be back to play in some regular season games. Don't know how many, though."

Rookie Josue De Paula shows promise in Ohtani's absence

In the meantime, rookie Josue De Paula has thrived in his first crack at the big leagues. He's only hitting .182, but the No. 6 prospect in baseball has drawn five walks with zero strikeouts in his first five games for an on-base percentage of .438. His first major league hit came on a towering 416-foot home run to right field in Miami on Sunday.

It's been a very small sample size, but he's been so effective that Roberts moved the 21-year-old from ninth in the order to the leadoff spot for Tuesday's game .

"I like the at-bats," Roberts said. "I like the at-bat quality. I understand it's a small sample, but that's kind of who he is as a hitter and for me, it'll be a good opportunity for him to get five at-bats tonight."

Though Roberts has emphasized that De Paula's on a "no promises" trial run, but he hasn't ruled out the possibility of his top prospect staying on after Ohtani returns and making the postseason roster as a lefty bat off the bench, or more.

"It's still very early as far as however many at-bats or plate appearances he's taken but in this small sample, it's been good. It's certainly a much different level of focus with the postseason, but baseball is still baseball," he said. "I hope he makes our decision hard."

articles.title: Fluminense into Copa Libertadores semifinals despite 2-1 loss at Platense
articles.summary: Despite a 2–1 loss to Argentina’s Platense on Tuesday, Brazil’s Fluminense secured a spot in the Copa Libertadores semifinals with a 3–2 aggregate victory....
articles.body:
BUENOS AIRES (AP) — Despite a 2–1 loss to Argentina 's Platense on Tuesday, Brazil 's Fluminense secured a spot in the Copa Libertadores semifinals with a 3–2 aggregate victory.

First-half goals from Guido Mainero (30') and Bruno Sepúlveda (45') brought the home team level at 2–2 on aggregate, before Agustín Canobbio struck in the 57th minute to score the decisive goal for the Brazilians.

Fluminense, the 2023 tournament champions, had taken control in the first leg at the Maracanã Stadium through goals from Nonato and Hulk.

This marks only the third time in Fluminense's history that they have reached the Copa Libertadores semifinals, following previous runs in 2008 and three years ago .

The defeat ends a fairytale campaign for surprise Platense, who came agonizingly close to reaching the semifinals for the first time.

Fluminense will face the winner of Wednesday's quarterfinal between Liga Deportiva de Quito and Palmeiras. In other action, Corinthians and Estudiantes will settle their 1–1 tie on Wednesday, before defending champions Flamengo take on Independiente del Valle on Thursday.

The Copa Libertadores final takes place on Nov. 28 at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo, Uruguay.

articles.title: Real Salt Lake's Diego Luna to miss rest of MLS season with torn meniscus
articles.summary: The 23-year-old attacker announced that his season in the MLS is over, with a return planned next year.
articles.body:
The season is over for Diego Luna , much earlier than the Real Salt Lake star had hoped.

The 23-year-old will undergo a procedure to repair a torn meniscus in his knee and will miss the rest of the season, he announced in an Instagram post.

"I haven't been the Diego Luna that many of you know. I want to apologize for everyone that has been supporting me and believes in me because through such a difficult year for me, there's been a constant battle within myself," Luna wrote. "That hasn't allowed me to express myself and reach my potential."

Real Salt Lake is winless in its last 11 matches in MLS play. Luna has played a part in most of those matches, including starting and going 70 minutes in a Sept. 9 loss at the Houston Dynamo . But he was listed on the injury report with a knee issue for a Sept. 12 defeat to New York City FC and now has vowed to get right for next season.

articles.title: Ravens Sign Former 71-Yard AFC North Weapon Before Saints Game
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are addressing concerns before facing the New Orleans Saints in Week 2.In their 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts, the Ravens...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are addressing concerns before facing the New Orleans Saints in Week 2.

In their 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts , the Ravens lost wide receivers Zay Flowers and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane to injuries. That raised questions about how the team would address the wide receiver position.

It appears the team has revealed its plan with the new announcement. Baltimore is bringing in reinforcements.

Baltimore Ravens Announce New Signing to the Team

The Ravens announced new roster moves on social media. They first announced that they have signed wide receiver Gage Larvadain to the practice squad. In a corresponding move, they also released kicker Jake Moody from the practice squad.

Moody joined the team after training camp amid concerns about Ravens kicker Tyler Loop's preseason kicking. Loop made all of his kicks against the Colts.

Larvadain spent last season with the Cleveland Browns , playing in 13 games. He finished with 7 receptions for 71 yards and 1 rushing attempt for 3 yards. Larvadain returned 24 punts for 167 yards, averaging 7 yards per return.

Ravens Add More Offensive Firepower After Latest Injuries

The Ravens needed more help at wide receiver, with so much uncertainty around Lane and Flowers. Lane could miss multiple games, while Flowers might miss a man-of-two games. Flowers is dealing with a hamstring injury from training camp, and Lane fractured his wrist.

Baltimore will lean on Rashod Bateman , Chris Moore , LaJohntay Wester , and rookie Elijah Sarratt, to step up at receiver if they are out. Moore could see himself going from the practice squad and staying on the active roster.

Larvadain may not ever see the field for the Ravens, but he at least gives them some insurance at wide receiver. He can also make an impact on special teams as a returner.

Baltimore could add more receivers in the future, but they still have plenty of talent that can help now. Moore and Wester stepped up in the Colts game. Bateman did not have as much impact in the contest.

Sarratt could see his reps increase dramatically in this game and might actually play. He could even be seen as a starter.

The Ravens would like to see more production from Bateman as the new WR1 receiver if Flowers is out. They have the room to survive over the next few weeks with the injuries they are dealing with.

This is not an ideal situation to face when the Saints are next on the calendar. The Ravens would much prefer to be healthy on offense after putting up over 500 yards on the Colts. Expect a healthy amount of carries in Week 2.

articles.title: Aces news: A‘ja Wilson provides injury update after missing FIBA World Cup
articles.summary: Team USA won gold during the 2026 FIBA World Cup, but they were missing a major piece of the team in Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson who opted out of playing...
articles.body:
Team USA won gold during the 2026 FIBA World Cup, but they were missing a major piece of the team in Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson who opted out of playing this go-round . With the Aces set to resume the WNBA season this week as they seek to defend their title, Wilson acknowledged that injury-wise, she didn't feel up to par in terms of playing, as per Brandy Flores of Las Vegas Sports Network.

"I'm feeling good. I'm feeling right where I need to be physically, I think it's just, it's a mental game. So I feel like I'm in a good space," Wilson said. "It was a major decision. I don't even think necessarily that it was getting ready for the postseason, it was just taking care of my body and what I need to do. This ball is going to stop bouncing eventually and I just want to make sure I at least feel good in that.

"I don't think I was thinking too much of, 'oh I got to get ready for the playoffs.' More so, I just don't feel well. And if I can't give myself 100 percent, I feel like I rob, not only my teammates, but wearing that uniform, that USA uniform. I didn't want to do that. That was the biggest thing, just not feeling 100 percent."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

A'ja Wilson had been dealing with a few nagging injuries during the course of the Aces' season thus far, but it seems like she's ready for the final stretch of the season.

The eight-time All-Star is in the running for her fifth MVP award, and has appeared in 37 games at just about 35 minutes per game. She's averaging 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 2.0 blocked shots with splits of 52.3 percent shooting from the field, 39.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 85.9 percent shooting from the free-throw line.

articles.title: Mile posts: Items on Jack Brown, Cody Baele, Niki Borner, Cody Baele, Kassie Parker, Lance Sobaski, Adam Gray, Lili Denton
articles.summary: Jack Brown fought off William Wadsley and Isaac Rankin to claim the 8K title in 26:00.4.
articles.body:
Central College seniors Jack Brown and William Wadsley and freshman Isaac Rankin look about as evenly matched as three teammates could be. Wadsley topped Brown, a Norwalk grad, by 6.1 seconds at the season-opening 6K Dutch Invite in Pella on Sept. 4. Rankin was 9.8 seconds behind Wadsley in that race.

Last weekend, at the 64th annual Les Duke Invite in Grinnell, it was Brown who fought off Wadsley, a Gilbert product, and ex-Knoxville runner Rankin to claim the 8K title in 26:00.4. Wadsley was just .4 of a second behind his teammate, who is the reigning NCAA mile indoor champion, with Rankin crossing the finish line in 26:00.9.

They lead off this edition of the WEEKEND UPDATE of the best performances by Iowa-based collegiate and post collegiate distance runners and triathletes.

Central showed it had much more than these three standouts in winning the team title with 16 points, just one off a perfect score. Freshman Carter Nunn claimed fourth overall in 26:19.6. Nunn hails from Marshalltown. Grinnell ended the Dutch's dominant run with Jack Lakin in fifth, but Central finished off the scoring with a sixth from ex-Norwalk runner Donovan Card, who ran 26:29.9. Grinnell was 45 points behind the Dutch.

William Penn senior Andrew Miller, an All-American in the NAIA 3,000 steeplechase final in May, claimed seventh in 26:41.4. Miller prepped at Pleasant Valley. Central junior James Brant, a former South Tama athlete, was next to finish in 26:43.8. Junior teammate Austin Vander Werf claimed ninth in 26:45.9. He attended Interstate 35 (Truro). The Central run continued with senior Mason Back in 11th in 26:55.6. Back went to Winterset. Former Lake Mills runner Knute Rogne, now a Central freshman, kept the Dutch run going by running 27:07.0. for 12th.

Central also won the women's team crown, but by a far less dominant spread. The Dutch scored 1-2-7-9-14 to win with 33 points, 13 ahead of host Grinnell. Central didn't have the individual champion, however, as Runablaze Iowa athlete Niki Borner, 40, of Indianola cruised to victory in the 6K race in 22:32.7, a 6:02.8 pace per mile. Borner is a former Bethel (MN) standout.

Settling for runner-up was Central College sophomore and former Dallas Center-Grimes prep Maddy Stevens in 23:01.5. Senior teammate Teah Miller, who prepped at Iowa Falls-Alden, ran 23:29.4 for third place. Grinnell junior Cindy Wang was the No. 2 finisher for the Pioneers in 23:52.0. Wang is an Iowa City West grad. Central true freshman Audrey Dummermuth, who starred at Johnston, took eighth in 24:00.1. A freshman paced Simpson College to third with 87 points. Former Indianola runner Ady Mason was ninth overall for the Storm in 24:01.2. Central freshman Morgan Back, sister of Mason, rounded out the top 10 in 24:01.5. The leader for William Penn was sophomore and former Central Springs prep Claire Rye in 12th in 24:12.1. Simpson freshman and former Woodward-Granger competitor Eva Fleshner grabbed 13th in 24:21.2. Her sophomore teammate, Ava Bussey, was next in 24:22.3. Bussey attended Council Bluffs Lewis Central. Central sophomore Bryann Wilson completed the top 15 in 24:23.2. Wilson competed for Ballard (Huxley).

Moving to the roads, where Des Moines man Cody Baele won the 44th annual Capital Pursuit 10-mile race for the second time in three years. The Fitness Sports Distance Project athlete rolled to victory at Easter Lake in 48:40.66. That time by Baele, 31, was just off his best at Capital Pursuit in 2024, when he ran 48:35.9. That time was No. 2 in Iowa road racing history, trailing only the 1985 mark of 48:03 by Clinton legend Phil Coppess at Pursuit.

Baele has run faster than Coppess' mark. He posted a personal-best 47:48 at the Cherry Blossom race in Washington, D.C., in April of 2024. That race is ineligible for Iowa records because it was held out of state. Baele won by more than 2:30 over Runablaze Iowa's Blake Whalen, 31, of Des Moines. Whalen, a Dubuque Senior and Iowa Central Community College grad, ran 51:22.60. He has run 50:09 at Capital Pursuit.

Recent Wartburg College grad Jack Kinzer, now a Driftless Distance Project athlete and living in Waverly, was third in his Capital Pursuit debut in 51:32.87. Kinzer, 23, is now a Wartburg cross country assistant coach. He is a Liberty High product. Taking fifth place was fellow Driftless runner Michael Goodenbour, also a former Wartburg runner. The ex-Cedar Falls runner, 23, was timed in 52:26.55. The Driftless run continued with former University of Dubuque runner Anthony Carney, 22, of Lake Geneva, Wisconsin, in sixth in 54:01.08.

Runablaze and Driftless alternated over the next four spots. Runablaze's Don Agisha, 22, of Norwalk, was seventh in 54:50.17. Former Urbandale and Simpson College runner Cole Leggett, a Driftless runner, was next to finish on a cool and rainy morning in 54:55.07. Runablaze's Artur Mueller, 43, of Davenport was the top masters finisher and ninth overall in 55:48.99.

Seven-time Loras College NCAA champion Kassie Parker, 27, took a break from her pursuit of the USATF Running Circuit season-long title to grab the women's title for a second consecutive year. The Crown Running athlete and ex-Clayton (Guttenberg) prep was just a few seconds off her winning effort of 59:00.39 from a year ago that was sixth best in Iowa history. Parker crossed the finish line in 59:07.54. Splitting Parker and runner-up Lexi Brown was Joshua Burbidge, 26, of Des Moines in 59:27.10. Brown, another ex-Wartburg runner who competed for New London in high school, took runner-up in the women's category in 1:00:08.10. Brown, 25, moves into the top 15 in Iowa history with that performance. Rob Semelroth, 51, of Des Moines was the second-best masters finisher in 1:00:28.03. Semelroth ran at Northern Iowa. Rounding out the top three in the women's race was former Newton and Drake University competitor Casey McDermott, 37, of Malcom in 1:00:25.99.

Runablaze's Pasca Cheruiyot, the 2024 winner of this race, took fourth in 1:01:01.29. The Ankeny woman, 40, moved into second in Iowa masters history. Next to finish was Runablaze teammate Melanie Hamilt, 31, of Iowa City in 1:01:40.01. Taking 19th was recent Wartburg grad Maddie Merna, now with the Driftless squad. Merna, 22, ran 1:02:28.14. The second-best female masters runner was Runablaze's Susie Duke, 46, of rural Searsboro. Duke was timed in 1:02:58.41. Runablaze teammate Lauren (Schulze) Wood, a former Valley prep, was 23rd overall in 1:03:24.64. Wood, 23, lives in Des Moines.

In the four-mile race, recent Wartburg grad Lance Sobaski of the Driftless squad was the winner in 19:03.30, a 4:45 pace per mile. The Des Moines man, 22, was NCAA runner-up in the 3,000 steeplechase in May. Sobaski cruised to victory over Runablaze's Karim Achengli Benmouais. The Urbandale man, 34, ran 20:28.99. Runablaze teammate Chase Bulten, 29, of Lehigh was third in 21:04.69. He is a Manson Northwest Webster and Northwestern College grad who started at Iowa Central. Former Drake runner Aziz Jdai, 26, captured fourth in 21:50.54. Ex-Waterloo West and Indian Hills Community College athlete Presley Berns, 20, of Evansdale was next to finish in 21:55.93. The women's winner was Runablaze athlete and former Southeast Warren and Simpson College competitor Elise Wieland, 26, of Des Moines in 24:43.23.

Moving briefly to track and field and the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, Hungary, over the weekend. Fourteen-time USATF national champion Shelby Houlihan, 33, competed in the women's 5,000 Sept. 13 and settled for 12th place in 15:18.65. The winner was Ethiopia's Likina Amebaw in 14:30.36. Houlihan is a 2016 Olympian who won 16 state titles competing for Sioux City East.

Luther College true freshman Adam Gray has a chance to be a four-time winner of the All-American Race hosted by the Norse. The Cedar Rapids Kennedy product won the men's four-mile race on Sept. 12 in 20:27.2. He topped senior teammate Michel Heinrich by 6.6 seconds. The Luther men won the team title with 32, six ahead of Iowa Central. Former Luther runner Kaeden Fellingham grabbed fourth in 21:04.3. Luther junior Jacob Bruns, another ex-Kennedy athlete, was fifth and the No. 3 scorer for the Norse in 21:11.9. Iowa City High grad Linus McRoberts, competing unattached, was next to finish in 21:31.3. A Luther Alumni runner, Tom Altier, secured seventh in 21:34.6. He attended Johnston. Taking a top-10 spot was Iowa Central freshman Anthony Valles, a Fort Dodge St. Edmond product, in ninth in 21:42.2.

Runablaze's Flannery Cerbin-Bohach is a past champion of the All-American Race hosted by Luther College in Decorah. This time, on Sept. 12, the former Norse runner settled for third place. The rural Cresco woman covered the 5K course in 19:26.9. Luther College true freshman Mia Deegan, a former Cedar Rapids Kennedy competitor, was fourth in 19:38.0. Wisconsin-Platteville took the victory with 42 points, 24 ahead of Luther. Third-place Iowa Central had the individual champion with freshman Zosia Zdobylak in 18:23.9.

Former Council Bluffs St. Albert runner Lili Denton continues to make a nice impact as a freshman for the University of Texas. Denton finished as the No. 2 athlete for the seventh-place Longhorns at the Texas A&M Invitational in College Station, Texas, on Sept. 11. Denton ran the 5K distance at the Watts Cross Country Course in 18:21.1, a 5:54.4 pace per mile. Texas' top finisher was five spots ahead of her. SMU took the team title with 21 points and sophomore Rose Mburu was the winner in 17:01.0.

Two Iowans finished in the top 25 at the WSU Cougar Classic XC Extravaganza in Colfax, Washington, on Sept. 11. Iowa City High grad Truman Thompson, a senior, crossed fifth for the Grizzlies in the 8K race in 25:31.3. He was just seven seconds off his PR. Montana was runner-up in the team race with 44 points, 27 behind Washington State. Junior Evans Kurui of Washington State was the champion in 22:36.8.

Former Southeast Polk prep Libby Hartz, a junior for the Montana women's team, secured 25th place in the 5K race in 19:55.7. Hartz also was the No. 5 finisher for the Grizzles, who ended up fourth in the team race with 77 points. Washington State won with a perfect score of 15 at Colfax Golf Course and Country Club. Freshman Millie Bii was the winner in 16:20.8.

Sophomore Emmett Swartzentruber looks like a pivotal member of the Black Hills State men's team. The Mid-Prairie (Wellman) product from Kalona was eighth overall and sixth on the winning team at the Gage McSpadden invite at the Fort Meade Facility in Sturgis, South Dakota, on Sept. 11. Swartzentruber claimed a new personal record for 6K of 19:14.8, a 5:09.7 pace per mile, as Black Hills State rolled to the team title with 20 points. Senior teammate Jaxon Straus was the winner in 18:50.6.

The flat course for the Dordt Sunflower Open is always a fast one and the meet Sept. 12 in Sioux Center was on par with past efforts. The host Defender women took the title of the five-team meet with just 20 points, 39 ahead of St. Mary (NE).

Taking runner-up honors behind sophomore teammate Joy Koole was Dordt sophomore Addison Liston. The Unity Christian (Orange City) product ran a new PR of 18:06.5 on the 5K course for a 5:49.7 pace per mile. Koole was the winner in 18:04.7. Northwestern College senior Emily DeGroot, an MOC-FV (Orange City) grad, was the leader for the Red Raiders in third in 18:21.2. Junior teammate Kayden Spencer, an Ogden native who first attended Des Moines Area Community College, ended up seventh in 18:54.9. Completing the top 10 was Dordt sophomore Elyse Zwart, a former Boyden-Hull athlete, in a new best of 19:11.8. Dordt senior Isabella Webb continued Dordt's deep run in 12th place in 19:17.9. Webb ran for Waukee High. Freshman teammate Katie Young was next to finish in 19:18.2. Young is a former Unity Christian runner. Defenders sophomore Raegan Snieder claimed 14th in 19:25.5. She competed for Pella High.

A former Dordt runner bested all of the collegians in the men's competition. Fitness Sports Distance Project's Jacob Vander Plaats claimed victory in the 6K race in 18:21.5, a 4:55.4 pace per mile. Vander Plaats is a Unity Christian product who won by 12.8 seconds.

The Dordt men took victory with a perfect 15 points, however, 38 ahead of Northwestern College. Running third for the Defenders and fourth overall was junior and former Le Mars Community performer Trace Obbink in 18:40.6. Senior teammate Caleb Van Beek, who attended Western Christian, was seventh in 18:47.4. Northwestern freshman Davis Johnson was the leader for the Red Raiders in eighth in 18:47.5. Johnson prepped at Ankeny Centennial. Yet another ex-Unity Christian athlete, freshman Tyler Rozenboom, rounded out the top 10 in 19:02.5. Rozenboom runs for Dordt. Junior teammate Brett Gifford, a former Dowling Catholic prep, was 13th in 19:09.2. Dordt grad Luke Swanson captured 14th in 19:09.2 and Derrek Vander Leest, another ex-Defender who has graduated, was the last of the 15 best finishers in 19:14.6.

Shifting to the Queen City Invite, where North Florida junior Cohen Kooker was the No. 5 finisher for the Ospreys. The Valley grad covered the Larry McAfee Course at McAlpine Park in Charlotte, North Carolina, in 18:39.6 for 28th place on Sept. 11. North Florida finished fourth in the team race with 88 points. The 5K winner was Marshall senior Rachael Withrow in 16:18.9.

Pleasant Valley grad Ani Wedemeyer and her Johns Hopkins squad stepped up against big schools at the Virginia Invitational on Sept. 11. The sophomore for the Division III program placed 47th in the 5K race at Panorama Farms in Earlysville, Virginia, in 18:56.3. Wedemeyer was sixth on the Blue Jays, who were fifth in the team race with 132 points, trailing North Carolina, Virginia, Wake Forest and William & Mary. Tar Heels junior Ciara O'Shea was the champion in 16:46.0.

Truman State junior Clare Stahr led the Bulldogs to the team crown at the Larry Young Invitational in Columbia, Missouri, on Sept. 11. The Gilbert product was fourth overall and the No. 2 runner in 19:10.1 for Truman State, which scored 26 points to easily top Park (Mo.) by 68 points in the 5K race at the Gans Creek Cross Country Course. Senior Hailey Gerard of Columbia (Mo.) was the leader in 18:27.5.

North Iowa Area Community College hosted the Trent Smith Invitational in Mason City on Sept. 12 and a Trojan runner was the 8K champion. North Iowa (Buffalo Center) grad Gavin Grunhovd, a NIACC sophomore, ran 26:16.7 to top ex-Iowa City West and Iowa Central athlete Seth Cheney by 26.6 seconds. Cheney competes for the FSDP squad.

Ankeny Christian Academy grad Alex Davis paced the third-place Faith Baptist squad. Davis ran 28:10.3 for fourth place. DMACC freshman Brady Sanger, who competed for Bondurant-Farrar, was fifth in 28:31.5. DMACC won the title with 24 points.

The DMACC women also claimed a title with 36 points, nine ahead of Faith Baptist. Ridge View (Holstein) product Addy Tesch was runner-up in the 5K in 19:41.0. Sophomore teammate Cece Thompson, who ran for Valley, was third in 20:55.6. The winner was Carlie Blevins of Faith Baptist in 19:34.4.

Milwaukee freshman Grace Storjohann took 47th overall for Milwaukee at the Phoenix Open in Green Bay, Wisconsin, on Sept. 12. The ex-Grundy Center prep ran 24:26.0 for the 6K distance and was the No. 4 finisher for Milwaukee, which was sixth in the team race. St. Thomas (MN) won the title with 28 points.

On to triathlon where former Cedar Rapids Washington and Luther College athlete Carson Christen placed ninth overall at Ironman Wisconsin in Madison on Sept. 13. Christen covered the 2.4-mile swim, 112-mile bike and 26.2-mile run in 9:25:12. His times were 56:20, 5:04:52 and 3:15:47 for those disciplines. Nathan Kim of the U.S. was the winner in 8:43:00.

Ending with the roads and the MVRA Benefit Classic half marathon in Dubuque. Former Loras College standout Joey Schultz, now with Runablaze, picked up second overall in 1:11:52. Schultz, 27, resides in Dubuque. Crown Running's Michael Eyres, a former Luther athlete, was next to finish in 1:13:43. Taking fourth overall and winning the women's crown was Runblaze's Amanda Edwards, 38, of Dubuque. The ex-Wartburg runner was timed in 1:29:26. The winner ran 1:11:25.

articles.title: OU football adds Bixby TE Connor Arant to 2028 recruiting class
articles.summary: OU football landed a commitment from 2028 Bixby four-star tight end Connor Arant on Tuesday.
articles.body:
NORMAN — Oklahoma football landed its second 2028 commitment.

Four-star tight end Connor Arant from Bixby High School committed to the Sooners on Tuesday, he told Rivals . Arant previously played at Jenks in 2024.

The 6-foot-6, 245-pounder chose OU over Alabama and Ohio State. He has visited the Sooners three times.

Arant is the No. 219 overall prospect, the No. 12 tight end and the No. 4 player in Oklahoma in the 2028 cycle, according to 247Sports' rankings.

He is teammates with four-star offensive tackle and fellow OU commit Kaeden Penny .

articles.title: ‘Tackling Malik Nabers’ — Adam Schefter Reveals John Harbaugh’s Unusual Test Before Giants Opener
articles.summary: Every athlete likes to be healthy. However, the price of pain and endurance often force players into taking the strongest possible measures to stay fit. So w...
articles.body:
Every athlete likes to be healthy. However, the price of pain and endurance often force players into taking the strongest possible measures to stay fit. So was the case of Malik Nabers after an injury temporarily out of action. Reports from the New York Giants' camp about events leading up to the franchise's Sunday opener against the Dallas Cowboys.

ESPN's Adam Schefter disclosed an unusual test that Nabers faced to prove his readiness for the game. Head coach John Harbaugh reportedly tackled the wideout to prove wideout could take a hit after knee surgery. The player apparently passed the unofficial test, paving way for his unofficial return to football action.

How Head Coach John Harbaugh Tackled Malik Nabers to Prove His Game-Readiness

In his first outing after the surgery, Nabers hauled in six catches for 69 yards. He probably has fewer other potential opportunities. He proved he was back, healthy, and was able to hit after scaling a grueling rehab process. And while his numbers may not be star-caliber, his performance Sunday night was one of the most encouraging to his growing fan base. However, an injury concern meant he won't make a decision on playing until roughly two hours before the game. Part of that decision-making process included receiving tackles from his head coach, per a recent report from Shefter.

In order to help Nabers mentally prepare for the game , Harbaugh reportedly devised a plan to ease Nabers' nerves. During the squad's walkthrough, the gaffer actually tried to tackle Nabers to prove the wideout could take hits. Fortunately, Nabers reportedly went down on Harbaugh's attempt (however weak or strong they were).

However, despite those preparations, Nabers still needed until Sunday night before ratifying he was truly ready to take the field. Clearly, Harbaugh's tackle attempt didn't fully convince the wideout to take the field, though it may have contributed. And the whole effort didn't impact Nabers at all, at least he had a fantastic story to tell after the contest.

Now that Nabers has finally eliminated the mental hurdle that preceded his first show, everything surrounding his complete return should be easier. Meanwhile, he'll be looking to surpass last season's statistics, which include 18 catches for 271 yards and touchdowns in 4 games.

Nabers caught six passes on nin e targets for 69 yards in the Giants' 28-20 win, his first game action since last September (2025). He reportedly was on the field for 36 out of 68 offensive plays. Only 11 of those were called runs.

Again, the head coach showed how d ifferent his approach could be in readying his players for the big moments. For a coach who has won 13 season openers since becoming a head coach in 2008, there's little surprise that he understands when players need nurturing or need pushing. This time, Nabers needed some pushing, and Harbaugh didn't hesitate to get Nabers over his insecurity about receiving hits during a game.

The Giants have an extra day to work with this week since they play on the road against the Los Angeles Rams next Monday night. And ahead of that game, Nabers and his global fanbase can rest assured that the athlete is now better prepared to face the game's rigors.

articles.title: Paul Sullivan: Mike Ditka’s return and Ben Johnson’s audacity liven up a Bears’ season
articles.summary: CHICAGO — News that Mike Ditka was back in Chicago and paying attention to the Bears from his Streeterville condo was almost as heartening as stories of Pope...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — News that Mike Ditka was back in Chicago and paying attention to the Bears from his Streeterville condo was almost as heartening as stories of Pope Leo XIV keeping up with the White Sox from the Vatican.

They're a couple of Chicago legends who did the unthinkable. One of them won a Super Bowl with the Bears , a feat which has never been repeated in 40 years. The other became the global leader of the Catholic Church, one of our biggest American religions after NFL football and sports gambling.

The pope and Ditka no doubt share a mutual interest in the Bears' quest for the Super Bowl, which is off to a rousing start after an opening week win over the Carolina Panthers .

Pope sightings have become the norm, with everyone making a trek to Rome to give him Chicago sports memorabilia. Ditka sightings have been rare, but Dan Pompei's summer visit to Ditka's domicile for an article in The Athletic was a reminder that Da Coach is still Da Coach.

The article portrayed an elderly Ditka enjoying his "coda" in Chicago after having moved back from Naples, Fla.

"Chicago is my home," Ditka tells Pompei, explaining his return.

Ditka has been out of the public eye for a while, and whenever that occurs, there are obvious concerns about that person's health. Especially if he's had a heart attack, two strokes, multiple hip replacement surgeries and other ailments, not to mention breaking his hand punching a locker in his second season as coach.

Asked what he should tell people about him, Ditka replies to Pompei: "Tell them I'm good."

A small group of friends, including former Bear Hall of Famer Dan Hampton, share old stories about the Bears and Ditka's days as a coach. Ditka's thoughts were brief. Pompei reports he "isn't as talkative as he used to be," adding "his eyes say what his words once did."

Since the visit was conducted before the Bears' opener, there was no reaction to the 59-point offensive performance by Caleb Williams and Co., or coach Ben Johnson going for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 21 in the second quarter.

Pompei did report that Ditka "likes Ben Johnson's style," which makes him like most everyone else in Chicago.

There was no mention of Hammond, or the idea of the Bears moving to a new stadium in Indiana, a possibility that might upset the coach if I'm guessing right. The mere idea of Ditka in a domed stadium in Hammond brought to mind the Minnesota "RollerDome" episode of 1987, where he insisted domes were "not meant for football" and "unfortunately, people waste a lot of money building them."

Now Chairman George McCaskey is on a dome-or-bust mission. Would Johnson wear rollerblades in the new Bears' dome?

Pompei's visit with the old coach isn't so much an interview as a tribute to Ditka, and to what he means to Chicago. It was eloquently done by Pompei, an old colleague from the Chicago Tribune, and I believe it's the first we've heard anything from Ditka himself in a few years.

Ditka's last public appearance at a Bears event was in June 2019 during the franchise's 100th anniversary celebration. He lived in Florida until apparently returning recently without fanfare.

Ditka deserves his privacy, and fortunately it sounds like his family is making sure he gets it. But hopefully the Bears can honor Ditka in some fashion soon, whether he's at Soldier Field or not. People deserve their flowers while they're still able to enjoy them.

The home opener Sunday against the Vikings at Soldier Field would be as good a time as any, with Bears fans already whipped into a frenzy following the offensive fireworks last Sunday during the win in Charlotte, N.C.

Hopefully Ditka was watching and remembering what it's like when the entire town is in your corner and the season starts on an ultra-high note.

Johnson, meanwhile, should bottle this feeling, since it's rare air in Chicago. The Bears completely wiped the contending Cubs and White Sox off most sports radio talk shows Monday, and made Johnson's Trump-ian decision to go for it on fourth down deep in his own territory a mere footnote in the big win.

Right now, Johnson can do no wrong, even when he's dead wrong. How long that lasts probably depends on the Bears' defense, which was less than stellar in the opener.

It seems obvious that after only one full season, Johnson is the most respected Bears coach since Ditka, albeit without much competition. The seven head coaches between Ditka and Johnson combined for four playoff wins, including three by Lovie Smith alone. It's been a minute since a head coach inspired Chicago.

So Johnson still has that new-car smell, and when you win like he did Sunday, you don't have to bother explaining your bad decisions.

"Yeah, I felt pretty good about it," he said about the call in his postgame news conference.

Case closed. Alleged masterminds don't apologize for their mistakes.

At least Johnson didn't join his index finger with his thumb, Ditka-style, and say: "See that, that's your IQ, buddy — zero."

The guess here is we'll probably see Johnson try something crazy again this season in another high-risk situation, doubling down on his audacity. Saying he wanted to break the all-time scoring record before the season even began was a hint of how smart Johnson thinks he is, and his belief in the offense.

We've never had a shortage in Chicago of managers, coaches, executives and owners who think they're the smartest guy in the room, but maybe Johnson is the real deal. And that's not necessarily a bad thing.

Ditka's ego was also well nourished when he was in his coaching prime here. Whatever works.

I don't recall the word "genius" attached to Ditka's name — his default setting was his toughness, as the "Iron Mike" nickname denotes. Johnson's persona is tied to a computer-like, offensive brain and an ability to motivate men with a T-shirt-ready slogan: "Good. Better. Best."

Johnson might not reach the status of a Chicago icon like Ditka.

articles.title: Breaking down the college sports act: A salary cap, a 'Lane Kiffin rule' and a superleague ban
articles.summary: The Senate took a key step this week toward passing a bill that would radically change college sports by instituting rules that would cover a wide range of t...
articles.body:
The Senate took a key step this week toward passing a bill that would radically change college sports by instituting rules that would cover a wide range of the multibillion-dollar industry, including how colleges pay their players and what those players can and cannot go to court to fight.

Senators voted 74-24 to close debate on The Protect College Sports Act, bringing it closer to a vote in that chamber. If it passes there, it would go to the House. Among the key provisions of the proposal:

The bill would put into law the revenue sharing that was negotiated under terms of the House settlement , which allows schools to share up to 22% of certain revenue with athletes. This year, that amounts to $21.58 million per school. It also would add a $27.5 million "retention pool" that can be used to keep current players on the roster and could diminish the amount of third-party name, image and likeness payments.

The bill offers the NCAA some protection against lawsuits in several areas, most notably eligibility issues that have landed the governing body in court dozens of times over the past year. Most recently, the lawsuits are coming from players who graduated high school in 2022 and were denied a fifth year of college eligibility under a new rule that kicks in for the Class of '23.

The legislation is intended to preempt state laws, many of which were passed over the past five years to regulate NIL within state borders, that conflict with the guidelines set by the national law. Exactly how this plays out could be subject to litigation.

The bill would generally limit athletes to one "free" transfer without having to sit out a season, in a move that could cut down on some of the chaos created by the transfer portal. Athletes went to court in recent years to win the right to transfer without penalty.

The bill would prohibit coaches from leaving one school for another during the season.

In a rewrite of a 1961 law that prohibited this, the legislation would give college athletic conferences the option of pooling their media rights in an effort to generate more revenue to fund their sports. The powerful Southeastern and Big Ten conferences don't agree it would make more money and have resisted this effort.

The bill would require most schools to maintain the same number of Olympic-sport programs as they had in the 2024-25 school year for at least nine years.

The measure would provide federal funding for broadband and media infrastructure at historically Black college and university programs.

The bill would also prohibit conferences from expanding beyond 19 teams and adds other measures to prevent the creation of a breakaway "superleague."
